3. What I Would Keep or Change in My Own Proposal (propostas/argon.md), and Why

What I would keep:

In-thread [COUNCIL-STATE-v1] status projection with valid_until_utc lease watermarks: Posting signed state blocks into the pinned chatgpt_intake_conversation_id from the PC when active remains the cleanest way for mobile GPT-6 Normal to answer status questions directly in-thread without requiring unverified mobile ChatGPT plugins or manual copy-pasting.   
MD

Stage 0 Capability Gate probes (CG-1–CG-4) and the Refutation Test 2 canary memory check for normal: Empirical verification of cross-device sync and cross-conversation memory isolation before launching a live debate remains essential under R7 and R8.   
MD

Strict channel/parser separation and .incomplete.md marker recovery: Treating propostas/ and revisoes/ as inert data and automatically staging .incomplete.md on missing markers (whose necessity was proven in Round 01 by sonnet.incomplete.md in MANIFESTO.md) should be kept in full.   
MD

What I would change, and why:

Replace continuous PC browser-polling (Path 1A) and raw GitHub file commits (Path 1B) with an outbound-polled HTTPS Council Relay (argon-R02-06): MANIFESTO.md revealed that during Round 01, Local browser use is disabled in Work settings blocked the PC coordinator's browser tools twice. Therefore, the PC worker must poll an external HTTPS Relay outbound (sol, sonnet, astra) for intake commands and King outputs rather than relying solely on scraping web threads in the PC browser.   
MD
+ 1

Change the single-turn Plan+Decree capture into a two-step Plan-Commit → Decree handshake (argon-R02-07): As sol, normal, and astra rightly identified, REGRAS.md requires DECISAO.md to cite the committed PLANO-FINAL.md SHA (C_plan), so PLANO-FINAL.md must be committed first and its commit SHA returned to Opus before DECISAO.md is finalized.   
MD

Move LEDGER.jsonl and periodic liveness_watermark heartbeats out of the Git repository (argon-R02-08): As sonnet noted, committing periodic heartbeats to Git creates repository noise and working-tree lock contention. Operational heartbeats and claim leases should live in the Relay and a local journal outside C:\Users\Martim\Documents\ChatGPT\Council, reserving Git commits exclusively for Council phase artifacts.   
MD
+ 1

Add sonnet's two-stage draft_request → confirm_launch(debate_id, context_commit) gate and pre-execution Sovereign Release/Veto/Amendment gate: My round 01 proposal jumped directly from LAUNCH_DEBATE to execution and treated sovereign veto/amendment as post-decree directives; holding launch until CONTEXTO.md is approved and holding decree execution until Martim releases/attests on the Relay is strictly safer under REGRAS.md and Law No. 2.   
MD

4. Open Disagreements and Missing Information That Could Change the Decision

Whether a worker-spawned local Codex process (codex app-server in sol/astra or codex exec in sonnet) can operate the existing coordinator's web browser channels (U1, R1, R2):

Disagreement / Unknown: sol, sonnet, and astra propose launching the Right Hand from a background worker via codex app-server or codex exec, while acknowledging it is unknown whether those non-interactive/server modes have access to the in-app browser tools used in Debate 002 and Round 01 of Debate 003 (and MANIFESTO.md shows browser access is also governed by the desktop Work settings toggle).   
MD

How it changes the decision: Stage 0 must run a non-destructive browser-action probe from the worker-launched Codex runtime (sonnet Stage 0(b) / astra Operator refutation test). If headless codex exec / codex app-server cannot drive the web participant channels, the worker must either attach to/message an active desktop Codex session or report blocked (awaiting_interactive_coordinator) whenever web participant rounds are dispatched.   
MD
+ 1

What mobile tool/connector capabilities actually work inside GPT-6 Normal on Martim's phone and account (U1, R1, R3, Criterion 4):

Disagreement: sonnet proposes custom MCP connectors on ChatGPT mobile (contradicted by OpenAI's help page cited by sol, normal, and astra); astra proposes Custom GPT Actions (which may switch the model away from GPT-6 Normal); normal proposes built-in Google Drive file creation/reading; sol proposes authenticated Relay web forms; argon proposes in-thread browser sync.   
MD

How it changes the decision: Stage 0 probes on Martim's actual phone in a GPT-6 Normal conversation will resolve whether any read/write connector (Google Drive or Actions) works without changing the model. If none can write directly from GPT-6 Normal, the one-tap signed Relay URL emitted by Normal (sonnet fallback + sol Relay) becomes the mandatory intake mechanism, and in-thread [COUNCIL-STATE-v1] posts (argon) + Relay status page (sol) becomes the mandatory status mechanism.   
MD
+ 1

Whether execution of DECISAO.md should start immediately after origin attestation or wait for an explicit Sovereign Release tap (R5, Law No. 2):

Disagreement: sol, normal, and astra require Martim to attest the origin of the King's decree (because provider connectors do not prove model identity), whereas sonnet combines origin confirmation with an explicit Sovereign Release Gate (confirm_release / confirm_veto / confirm_amend) so Martim can inspect the committed decree before irreversible execution begins.   
MD

How it changes the decision: Since Martim already has to perform a one-tap origin attestation on the Relay for security (sol, normal, astra), combining that attestation tap with sonnet's release/veto/amend options on the same confirmation screen resolves both provenance and pre-execution veto capability in a single step.   
MD

All five proposals converge on the same assumption for U2: the PC must be powered on, logged into an active user session with required permissions (Local browser use enabled in Work settings for web rounds), connected to the network, and running the local worker; while unavailable, requests remain queued in the Relay and status reports CURRENT_PC_STATE: UNAVAILABLE alongside the last-known recorded state. Martim's acceptance of this operating condition locks in U2.

Risks and checks

Risk of Headless Codex Lacking Web Coordinator Browser Tools (argon-R02-02, argon-R02-04, argon-R02-13 — threatens R1, R2, R8):

Failure condition: The Windows worker claims a request from the Relay and invokes codex app-server or codex exec, but the spawned process cannot drive the in-app browser sessions for ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, or Work settings has disabled local browser use.   
MD

Check and result that changes the recommendation: Run a Stage 0 probe before building the full bridge: have the local worker start a test turn via codex app-server and codex exec and attempt a read-only browser state check. If neither headless path can access the browser tools, change the worker adapter so it injects/dispatches the task into an active interactive Codex desktop coordinator session and reports BLOCKED (BROWSER_TOOL_DISABLED_OR_UNAVAILABLE) in Relay status whenever that session or Work settings browser toggle is inactive.   
MD

Risk of Mobile ChatGPT Connector Failure or Model Substitution (argon-R02-01, argon-R02-03, argon-R02-09, argon-R02-12 — threatens R1, R3, Criterion 4):

Failure condition: Custom MCP tools do not appear on ChatGPT mobile (sonnet), Custom GPT Actions force switching away from GPT-6 Normal (astra), or Google Drive file creation fails in mobile chat (normal).   
MD

Check and result that changes the recommendation: Test GPT-6 Normal on Martim's phone in Stage 0. Unless a native action works directly inside GPT-6 Normal without changing the model, lock in the zero-plugin baseline: (a) for intake, Normal outputs a pre-filled markdown link to the authenticated Relay confirmation page (one tap by Martim to submit); (b) for status, the PC operator posts [COUNCIL-STATE-v1] snapshots directly into chatgpt_intake_conversation_id when active, backed by the Relay status page when the PC is offline.   
MD

Risk of Invalid Plan Commit Citation or Unchecked Decree Execution (argon-R02-07, argon-R02-10 — threatens R5, R8, REGRAS.md):

Failure condition: DECISAO.md is generated before PLANO-FINAL.md is committed to Git, or a decree is executed before Martim attests its origin and releases it.   
MD

Check and result that changes the recommendation: Enforce in the Relay state machine that submit_decree is rejected unless plan_commit_sha is already recorded from a verified Git commit of PLANO-FINAL.md, and that the worker cannot transition a decree to executing without a signed sovereign confirm_release (or confirm_amend) record bound to (debate_id, plan_commit_sha, decree_sha256).   
MD

Risk of Cross-Conversation Memory or Shared Connector Contamination of normal (argon-R02-05 — threatens R7):

Failure condition: Account-level memory or an active Google Drive/MCP connector in ChatGPT allows participant normal's fresh advisory conversation to recall mobile intake/status discussions or read Council artifacts during an open round.   
MD

Check and result that changes the recommendation: Run argon's canary phrase probe (Refutation Test 2) and verify that all external connectors are disabled/unselected in normal's advisory web conversation before dispatching PACOTE-PROPOSTA.md or PACOTE-REVISAO.md.

## revisoes/sonnet.md

END-OF-PACKET-003-REVIEW-v1 | Missing sections: none

Review — sonnet
Participant: sonnet.
Visible model: Sonnet 5.5 per the session configuration. The interface label is not visible to me and is not independently attested.
Date: 2026-10-17.
Phase and round: Cross review / round 02.
Context version: v1 (debate 003-mobile-bridge).
Reference commit: source baseline 95d853ba7480260d5a9c4b8541b4b1b32a6d90f3; governance 389a4367de088361adcaeec271fb438c6fb0b492.
Files received and read: all sixteen listed sections, in the stated order and in full: LEIS, REGRAS, CONTEXTO, OPERATING-MODEL, MANIFESTO, CONTRIBUICAO template, the five proposals, sonnet.incomplete.md, the three link captures, FIXED-PHASE-PROMPT. None partial.
Tools used: none. I retrieved no documentation in this phase, so no external capability claim below was independently verified. Each is carried as attributed, contested or unknown.
Cross-conversation memory: an account-level memory snapshot exists in this deployment. Nothing in it concerns this debate and I did not use it.
Prior exposure: this packet only. The packet contains propostas/sonnet.md and sonnet.incomplete.md, labelled as sonnet’s. I do not recognize them from this conversation, since it is new, so I cannot confirm authorship. Their content is consistent with the participant ID, and I review them by the same standard as the others.
New conversation: yes, as far as I can observe. The packet and routing line were the first content.
Access limits:
No phone, account or PC inspection.
Rendered captures carry interface artifacts: argon’s “MD” and “+ 1” labels, argon table cells cut mid-text, and a stray citation fragment inside sonnet.incomplete.md.
Normal’s capture has no link list, so its external sources cannot be traced to URLs.
Brief

Position, not a plan. Keep what the proposals share:

an outbound-only PC worker;
an append-only operational ledger bound to debate and revision;
Git as the artifact record;
a plan-commit-then-decree handshake;
Martim-authenticated origin attestation before any decree executes.

Treat every phone-side adapter as a candidate that must pass a probe in the exact intended conversation before it is chosen. The candidates are a native tool in the GPT-6 Normal conversation, a Claude remote connector, Drive/Gmail, and an explicit relay page.

Decisive reasons:

No proposal establishes a phone-side read or write path in the intended conversations.
The ChatGPT-side evidence conflicts: sol, normal and astra cite a help page saying custom MCP is web-only, while sonnet cites an SDK page saying connectors reach mobile once linked on web.
The choice is therefore decided by authority and recovery, where sol, normal and astra are strongest, and by surface fidelity, where astra and sonnet are strongest.

Blocking defects:

sonnet and argon both produce decrees that cannot cite the plan’s commit, contrary to REGRAS “Decision”.
argon’s transport depends on UI polling, its fallback replaces the specified entry surface, and its status path has no fallback.

Main alternative: argon’s browser-sync design, the only one needing no new connector. It fails if conversation sync or unattended browser control is unreliable. MANIFESTO records a Work setting that disabled the browser tool, and a clipboard that returned empty then stale content.

Decisive check: probe in the exact Normal and Opus phone conversations, and run an unattended Right Hand start that reaches a web participant.

Adds a state and a Martim action on boundary 1, unless Martim states that the request itself is the authorization.
2. Comparison against requirements and criteria

Design discriminators

Dimension	sol	normal	argon	sonnet	astra
Phone → PC	Paste into an authenticated relay form	ChatGPT writes a Drive document	PC polls the intake conversation	MCP tool in ChatGPT	GPT Action
State → phone	Martim pastes a snapshot	Drive read	Snapshots posted into the thread	get_status tool	Action status call
Synthesis → Claude	Remote connector, attachment fallback	Drive document, manual open	PC drives the Claude web thread	MCP parts	Remote connector
Decree → PC	Connector or upload, attested	Gmail, attested	Scraped from Claude web	MCP submit, release gate	Connector, attested
PC trigger	Windows worker plus app server	Drive change feed plus worker	Daemon	Courier plus codex exec	Supervisor plus app server
Authority root	Martim attestation	Martim attestation	Pinned conversation plus nonce	Scope plus release tap	Martim attestation

R#, by design

R#	sol	normal	argon	sonnet	astra
R1	met	met	unverified	met	met
R2	met	met	met	met	met
R3	unverified	unverified	unverified	met	met
R4	met	met	met	met	met

R7	met	met	met	met	met
R8	met	unverified	unverified	unverified	met

These codes assess the design against the requirement as written. Capability dependencies appear under U1 and R8, and in the Evidence table.

By priority

Authority and complete delivery.
sol, normal and astra are strongest. Each has the plan-commit-then-decree handshake and an attestation bound to the exact digest.
sonnet has the best launch authorization but loses points on ordering and on scope-as-role.
argon is weakest, because it has no attestation and executes on capture.
Demonstrated capability.
argon rests on operations Debate 002 demonstrated, but its sync assumption is unestablished and MANIFESTO records the browser tool failing.
The others rest on documented but unverified connectors.
sol, astra and sonnet each name the unverified Codex tool-parity dependency. argon, which keeps browser control on the PC, does not.
State and recovery.
astra’s four dimensions and sonnet’s server-side pc_current are the clearest.
Every proposal except argon has a reconciliation state for uncertain effects.
argon’s write-ahead log addresses the same problem differently.
Fit to surfaces.
sonnet, astra and argon answer status directly in Normal.
sol keeps Normal but needs manual transfers.
normal keeps Normal but adds Drive and Gmail.

No proposal estimates cost, effort or resources, apart from the minor phrase in sonnet-R02-10.

3. Current recommendation

What I would carry forward

A transport-independent contract layer. This means:
an envelope with debate, revision, idempotency key and payload digest;
authenticated principal supplied by the server, never by payload text;
append-only records, and separate state dimensions;
freshness computed at read time;
a reconciliation_required or outcome_unknown state for interrupted effects.
Authority. Authentication is not authorship. Before any decree executes, Martim authenticates an attestation bound to the exact digest and conversation reference. His veto and amendment are separate records created only through his authenticated action.
Sequence. The sequence runs plan, commit, return the commit reference to the King, decree citing it, then execution and King review.
Context. A launch authorization bound to a context commit is carried forward, unless Martim states otherwise (sonnet-R02-19).
Phone-edge adapters. Each is a candidate that must pass a probe in the exact conversation:
a native read/write tool in GPT-6 Normal;
a Claude remote connector;
Drive/Gmail;
the sol relay-page baseline, kept as a labelled fallback.
No adapter replaces a specified surface without Martim’s instruction.
PC trigger. An outbound-only worker, with “required tools and settings present” as a checked precondition and a visible blocked state (sonnet-R02-17).
From argon. Keep the Stage 0 report, the lease idea (computed at read time), the canary exposure test and the parser separation. Keep browser-sync as a probe candidate, not as the primary trigger.

Decisive gaps raised by one proposal

astra (surface fidelity). The ChatGPT adapter must run in the GPT-6 Normal conversation, and a custom GPT or another model must not be renamed “Normal”. This holds. It also applies to every ChatGPT-side adapter in the other proposals, including mine.
argon (liveness lease). Valid, but it needs a clock the model may not have (sonnet-R02-18).
normal (Drive change feed plus readback). A documented receiving primitive, usable if Normal’s Drive write and Claude’s return path are verified. Their state is unknown.
This review (sonnet-R02-17). The only evidence the packet holds about unattended browser availability is the MANIFESTO episode. No proposal addresses it.
4. What I would keep or change in my own proposal

Keep

The relay-plus-courier shape.
Separate OAuth clients and scopes.
The Stage 0 probes.
The launch confirmation bound to a commit.
Receipt matching.
Server-side pc_current.
The journal and reconcile-before-rerun rule.
The @codex analysis.

Change

Add the plan-commit-then-decree two-step (sonnet-R02-13).
Add Martim’s origin attestation and stop treating scope as role (sonnet-R02-14).
Downgrade the mobile-connector row to contested. Add the exact-conversation probe, including the model label, and sol’s relay-page baseline as a named fallback (sonnet-R02-15).
Add a Stage 0 check of the browser setting and an explicit blocked state (sonnet-R02-17).
State the release-gate rule as a premise for Martim, with both modes supported (sonnet-R02-16).
Replace mirror-sourced claims with primary pages, or leave them attributed.

# Review — astra

- **Participant:** astra.
- **Visible model:** Not independently visible. Requested `gpt-6-astra`, reasoning effort `high`, is configuration metadata, not model attestation.
- **Date:** 2026-10-17.
- **Phase and round:** Review / round 02.
- **Context version:** v1.
- **Reference commit:** `95d853ba7480260d5a9c4b8541b4b1b32a6d90f3`.
- **Closed proposal set:** `730f578ee8a32aa22a5d1310524cc990db26f683`, as identified by the packet.
- **Files received and read:** All supplied sections: Laws, rules, context, operating model, manifest, contribution template, proposals by sol, normal, argon, sonnet and astra, `sonnet.incomplete.md`, all three source-link inventories, and the fixed review prompt. No section was omitted.
- **Tools used:** Official web search and retrieval through `web__run`, orchestrated by `functions.exec`. An attempted environment-required OpenAI documentation skill read through `exec_command` failed before process execution; no local file contents were obtained.
- **Cross-conversation memory:** General workspace guidance was injected by the environment. It was not used as Council evidence. No memory files were retrieved.
- **Prior exposure:** This review packet only within this execution. I recognize `propostas/astra.md` as the proposal attributed to my participant ID; I do not claim independent recollection of its execution.
- **New conversation:** Fresh advisory execution according to the transport instruction; separate from the coordinator.
- **Access limits:** No repository inspection, phone/account inspection, integration tests, implementation, file changes, services, external messages or decree. Documentation establishes product primitives, not Martim’s actual access.

## Brief

My current preference is **Normal’s Drive intake/status mechanism as a conditional candidate**, retaining the explicit origin checks and plan-commit handshake described by Sol and Astra. Official sources support the underlying Drive actions and change feed. Exact mobile operation remains unknown.

Sol provides the clearest explicit manual transport alternative, but its status path requires Martim to retrieve and transfer a snapshot. That cannot silently become the interpretation of asking Normal for status.

I would withdraw my proposal’s preference for GPT Actions until the specified Normal conversation/model is demonstrated to support them. Documented mobile custom-GPT use does not establish that compatibility.

Argon’s browser approach is conditional on more than conversation synchronization: the autonomous worker must possess the browser interfaces, distinguish human commands from automation-written messages, and implement atomic command admission. Its proposed fallback also requires independent verification.

Sonnet’s direct ChatGPT MCP claim is not supported by the official sources inspected. Its decree sequence additionally omits returning the committed plan reference to the King before decree issuance. Connector scopes establish permissions, not Opus authorship.

The shared decisive gap is the local execution boundary: starting Codex does not establish that the resulting task can operate the existing coordinator’s channels.

No proposal is demonstrated end to end. These are recommendations to the King, not a bridge selection or final plan.

## Assessment convention

**Met** means the written design explicitly satisfies the requirement’s specification. It does not mean deployment acceptance has passed. **Broken** identifies a contradiction or missing necessary operation in the written design. **Unverified** means a decisive capability, interpretation or enforcement mechanism remains unresolved.

Evidence identifiers refer to the table below. All objections are raised in review round 02.

## Shared objection

This objection applies to every proposal and should retain one ID throughout synthesis.

| ID | Target: file, section, passage | Type | Severity | Failure condition | Consequence | Basis and phase | Correction or test | Effect on the decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| astra-R02-01 | All proposals: worker/daemon/courier/supervisor starts the existing coordinator | Integration | blocking | The independently started task lacks the coordinator’s browser tools, authenticated sessions or required permissions | A request reaches the PC but the Council workflow cannot proceed autonomously | Operating model, missing boundaries; E6 and E7; review 02 | From an inactive coordinator state, demonstrate the chosen receiver starting the intended task in the specified checkout and operating the required existing channels. Record permission failures explicitly | No candidate qualifies as an executable complete bridge until this passes |

Sol, Sonnet and Astra identify this gap explicitly. Normal requires a supported invocation but leaves its adapter unspecified. Argon’s historical browser evidence does not establish daemon access to those interfaces.

Argon’s autonomous browser access is not established by the historical active-coordinator evidence |
| **3. Correct state and recovery** | Sol, Normal, Sonnet and Astra explicitly acknowledge uncertain external effects. Argon requires stronger atomic admission details. Every candidate still needs actual interruption, duplicate and amendment checks |
| **4. Fit to the specified surfaces** | Normal’s design would preserve direct mobile intake/status if its account-specific checks pass. Sol’s manual status path requires explicit acceptance. Astra must avoid replacing Normal with a different GPT. Sonnet must establish mobile tools. Argon must prove both synchronization and authorized autonomous operation |

No proposal passes all acceptance requirements on current evidence. This conclusion is not a vote or an inference from provider agreement.

## Current recommendation

I would recommend that the King retain **Normal’s Drive intake/status route as the leading conditional transport candidate**, because the reviewed primary sources support its underlying operations and receiving mechanism. This is not evidence that Martim’s phone session supports them.

I would retain Sol’s authenticated manual relay as a clearly labelled alternative, conditional on Martim accepting its status handoff. I would not describe manual phone transport as eliminating PC automation: after valid admission, the worker may still operate automatically.

For authority and revision handling, I would retain the exact-artifact origin attestation and committed-plan handshake described by Sol, Normal and Astra. Sonnet’s permission scopes and Argon’s pinned channels remain useful controls, but neither establishes authored origin.

A decisive distinction emphasized by my proposal deserves explicit treatment: **successful operation in a custom GPT or a different model does not establish operation in the specified Normal conversation**. A generic mobile capability test is insufficient.

The recommendation remains conditional on **astra-R02-01** and the relevant phone checks. There is no basis to declare a complete bridge operational.

## What I would change in my own proposal

I would:

- Retain the broker/supervisor separation, origin receipt, revision checks and recovery contracts.
- Remove GPT Actions as the preferred adapter until **astra-R02-14** is resolved.
- Include Normal’s documented Drive route as a serious direct-interface candidate.
- Preserve the manual alternative without assuming it satisfies Martim’s intended R3 interaction.
- Make the amendment check concrete: after accepting a superseding instruction, a disconnected or replaced worker must not continue under obsolete authorization. Test that enforcement around actual effects rather than relying only on a “stop” message.
- Require packet acceptance checks to omit a middle section while retaining valid outer markers. Marker success alone must not produce a complete-delivery claim.

These are revisions to my advice, not edits to the original proposal.

## Evidence and assumptions

All external sources below were consulted during **review round 02**.

| ID / decisive claim | State | Provenance and passage | Phase | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **E1:** The inspected documentation does not establish Sonnet’s claimed custom-MCP mobile path | supported | [OpenAI custom MCP help](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/12584461-connecting-custom-mcp-servers-in-chatgpt), availability/mobile FAQ; [current connection guide](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/deploy/connect-chatgpt), connection/testing sections | Review 02 | The help page specifies web availability; the connection guide does not substantiate the claimed mobile propagation. This does not prove every plugin mechanism is unavailable |
| **E2:** ChatGPT documents Google Drive creation/update actions, conditional on permissions and configuration | supported | [Google Drive setup](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10929079-google-workspace-admin-managed-setup), conversation actions and permissions; [Google data controls](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10408842-google-app-data-controls-faq), Drive scopes | Review 02 | General functionality, not the intended phone/model combination. The Drive-specific documentation also prevents treating a generic search-only statement as universal |
| **E3:** Drive supplies a concrete change-retrieval mechanism | supported | [Google: Retrieve changes](https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/guides/manage-changes), continuation tokens and notifications | Review 02 | Notifications indicate changes exist; the receiver must retrieve and process them |
| **E4:** Claude documents Drive retrieval and Gmail sending; Gmail attachment content is not directly exposed | supported | [Claude Google Workspace connectors](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10166901-use-google-workspace-connectors), capabilities and limitations | Review 02 | Supports Normal’s primitives; does not verify exact phone operation or unchanged document delivery |
| **E5:** Claude documents mobile web connectors and cloud-origin remote-MCP connections | supported | [Connector availability](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11176164-use-connectors-to-extend-claude-s-capabilities); [remote MCP network requirements](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11175166-get-started-with-custom-connectors-using-remote-mcp) | Review 02 | Supports the mechanism, not Opus authorship, account access or complete packet receipt |
| **E6:** Codex App Server documents starting/resuming threads and starting turns | supported | [Codex App Server](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server), lifecycle overview | Review 02 | Establishes a programmatic trigger primitive; not inheritance of the coordinator’s browser interfaces |
| **E7:** No complete mobile bridge or autonomous replacement runtime is demonstrated in this packet | supported | Supplied operating model, missing boundaries; proposal access-limit declarations | Review 02 | Evidence limit only. Historical coordinator success remains attributed to the supplied operating record |
| **E8:** Custom-GPT operation is not equivalent to ordinary mobile conversation integration | supported | [GPTs in ChatGPT](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8554407-gpts-in-chatgpt), mobile invocation and creation restrictions; [Actions configuration](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9442513-configuring-actions-in-gpts), model/workspace restrictions | Review 02 | The mobile ordinary-chat `@` flow is unavailable; new personal-account GPT creation is restricted. Martim’s applicable configuration is unknown |
| **E9:** A decree must cite the committed plan | supported | Supplied `REGRAS.md`, “Decision” | Review 02 | Contract requirement; a source-set commit or uncommitted plan record is insufficient |
| **E10:** Connector credentials or pinned channels establish Opus authorship | unknown | No inspected provider mechanism establishes this exact provenance | Review 02 | Do not promote authenticated access into verified royal origin |
| **E11:** Proposed ledgers and admission controls satisfy their stated contracts | assumption | Architecture and recovery sections of the proposals | Review 02 | Requires implementation and observed acceptance; no tests were performed here |

## Open disagreements and missing information

1. **R3 interpretation:** Whether Martim accepts transferring a recorded snapshot into Normal, or requires Normal to retrieve it directly when asked.
2. **Exact mobile capabilities:** Available read/write actions in the specified Normal and Opus conversations, including actual model selection and permissions.
3. **Worker interfaces:** The supported route from an accepted command to a fully equipped Right Hand task.
4. **Authority identities:** The permitted request writers, authenticated sovereign channel, intended King conversation and exact-artifact attestation procedure.
5. **PC availability:** U2 remains an explicit condition. Stored acceptance must remain distinguishable from PC receipt and execution.
6. **Recovery enforcement:** Atomic admission, interruption after an external effect, and rejection of obsolete execution after an amendment.
7. **Full delivery:** Actual content reaching the intended King conversation, including recovery from missing interior material despite intact markers.

Resolving these facts could change the preferred transport. Until then, the evidence supports conditional designs and specific corrections, not a decree.

END-OF-CONTRIBUTION

data-path-to-node="25">2.3 Message Schemas, State Machine, and Idempotency Rules (R3, R5, R6, R8)</h4><ol start="1" data-path-to-node="26"><li><p data-path-to-node="26,0,0"><b data-path-to-node="26,0,0" data-index-in-node="0">Request &amp; Sovereign Directive Envelope (<code data-path-to-node="26,0,0" data-index-in-node="40">COUNCIL-REQUEST-v1</code> / <code data-path-to-node="26,0,0" data-index-in-node="61">SOVEREIGN-DIRECTIVE-v1</code>):</b></p><ul data-path-to-node="26,0,1"><li><p data-path-to-node="26,0,1,0,0">Required fields: <code data-path-to-node="26,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="17">schema</code>, <code data-path-to-node="26,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="25">request_id</code>, <code data-path-to-node="26,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="37">idempotency_key</code> (<code data-path-to-node="26,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="54">sha256(debate_id + command + target_revision + payload_digest)</code>), <code data-path-to-node="26,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="119">debate_id</code>, <code data-path-to-node="26,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="130">command</code> (<code data-path-to-node="26,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="139">LAUNCH_DEBATE</code> | <code data-path-to-node="26,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="155">REOPEN_ROUND</code> | <code data-path-to-node="26,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="170">APPROVE_DECREE</code> | <code data-path-to-node="26,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="187">VETO_DECREE</code> | <code data-path-to-node="26,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="201">AMEND_DECREE</code>), <code data-path-to-node="26,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="216">author</code> (<code data-path-to-node="26,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="224">Martim</code>), <code data-path-to-node="26,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="233">target_revision_sha</code>, <code data-path-to-node="26,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="254">pc_availability_condition</code> (<code data-path-to-node="26,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="281">PC_ONLINE_DAEMON_ACTIVE</code>), <code data-path-to-node="26,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="307">body</code>, <code data-path-to-node="26,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="313">nonce</code>.</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="26,0,1,1,0"><b data-path-to-node="26,0,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="0">Idempotency rule (R6):</b> Before executing any command, <code data-path-to-node="26,0,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="53">council-bridge</code> scans <code data-path-to-node="26,0,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="74">debates/&lt;debate-id&gt;/LEDGER.jsonl</code>. If <code data-path-to-node="26,0,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="111">request_id</code> or <code data-path-to-node="26,0,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="125">idempotency_key</code> already exists with status <code data-path-to-node="26,0,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="168">ACCEPTED</code>, <code data-path-to-node="26,0,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="178">EXECUTING</code>, or <code data-path-to-node="26,0,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="192">COMPLETED</code>, the daemon does <b data-path-to-node="26,0,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="219">not</b> start a second task; it re-emits <code data-path-to-node="26,0,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="256">[COUNCIL-ACK-v1]</code> citing the existing state and commit SHA.</p></li></ul></li><li><p data-path-to-node="26,1,0"><b data-path-to-node="26,1,0" data-index-in-node="0">Recorded State Contract (<code data-path-to-node="26,1,0" data-index-in-node="25">STATE.json</code> and <code data-path-to-node="26,1,0" data-index-in-node="40">[COUNCIL-STATE-v1]</code> for R3 &amp; U2):</b></p><ul data-path-to-node="26,1,1"><li><p data-path-to-node="26,1,1,0,0">Required fields:</p><ul data-path-to-node="26,1,1,0,1"><li><p data-path-to-node="26,1,1,0,1,0,0"><code data-path-to-node="26,1,1,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="0">debate_id</code>, <code data-path-to-node="26,1,1,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="11">context_version</code>, <code data-path-to-node="26,1,1,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="28">governance_baseline_sha</code>, <code data-path-to-node="26,1,1,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="53">head_commit_sha</code>, <code data-path-to-node="26,1,1,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="70">plan_commit_sha</code>, <code data-path-to-node="26,1,1,0,1,0,0" data-index-in-node="87">decree_commit_sha</code></p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="26,1,1,0,1,1,0"><code data-path-to-node="26,1,1,0,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="0">phase</code> (<code data-path-to-node="26,1,1,0,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="7">INTAKE</code> | <code data-path-to-node="26,1,1,0,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="16">PROPOSALS_OPEN</code> | <code data-path-to-node="26,1,1,0,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="67">REVIEWS_CLOSED</code> | <code data-path-to-node="26,1,1,0,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="84">SYNTHESIS_HANDOFF</code> | <code data-path-to-node="26,1,1,0,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="104">DECREED</code> | <code data-path-to-node="26,1,1,0,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="114">EXECUTION</code> | <code data-path-to-node="26,1,1,0,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="126">KING_REVIEW</code> | <code data-path-to-node="26,1,1,0,1,1,0" data-index-in-node="140">COMPLETED</code>)</p></li><li><p data-path-to-node="26,1,1,0,1,2,0"><code data-path-to-node="26,1,1,0,1,2,0" data-index-in-node="0">operational_state</code> (<code data-path-to-node="26,1,1,0,1,2,0" ## capturas/sonnet-incomplete-rendered.html

<div data-perf-reply-text="" class="_blocks_4za3l_47 standard-markdown grid-cols-1 grid [&amp;_&gt;_*]:min-w-0 whitespace-normal break-words print:block"><p dir="ltr">END-OF-PACKET-003-PROPOSAL-v1 | Missing sections: none</p>
<h2 dir="ltr">Proposal — sonnet</h2>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li><strong>Participant:</strong> sonnet</li>
<li><strong>Visible model:</strong> Sonnet 5.5, taken from the session configuration. The interface label is not visible to me and is not independently attested.</li>
<li><strong>Date:</strong> 2026-10-17</li>
<li><strong>Phase and round:</strong> Proposals, round 01</li>
<li><strong>Context version:</strong> v1 (debate 003-mobile-bridge)</li>
<li><strong>Reference commit:</strong> source baseline 95d853ba7480260d5a9c4b8541b4b1b32a6d90f3; governance 389a4367de088361adcaeec271fb438c6fb0b492</li>
<li><strong>Files received and read:</strong> all seven sections, read in full: LEIS, REGRAS, CONTEXTO, OPERATING-MODEL, MANIFESTO, CONTRIBUICAO template, fixed phase prompt. None partial.</li>
<li><strong>Tools used:</strong> WebSearch (standard mode), six queries on ChatGPT custom MCP connectors, Claude remote MCP and mobile, Codex GitHub triggers, <code dir="ltr">codex exec</code>, GitHub self-hosted runners, and Claude/GitHub connectors. Only search-result excerpts were read; no page was fetched in full. Several excerpts came from third-party mirrors, noted in the evidence table.</li>
<li><strong>Cross-conversation memory:</strong> account-level memory exists in this deployment. Nothing in it concerns this debate and I did not use it.</li>
<li><strong>Prior exposure:</strong> none beyond this packet.</li>
<li><strong>New conversation:</strong> yes, as far as I can observe. The packet and routing line were the first content.</li>
<li><strong>Access limits:</strong> I cannot test Martim’s ChatGPT or Claude accounts, plans, phones or PC. Every capability claim is about documentation, not Martim’s setup.</li>
</ul>
<h3 dir="ltr">Brief — up to 300 words</h3>
<p dir="ltr"><strong>Recommendation.</strong> Build one small public HTTPS MCP server, the <strong>relay</strong>, with an append-only ledger. Attach it as a custom connector to both phone apps: ChatGPT for intake and status, Claude for the King. Add an outbound-only <strong>courier</strong> on the PC. The courier claims work from the relay and starts the existing Right Hand with <code dir="ltr">codex exec</code>. The relay is the control plane for requests, state, packet parts, decrees and execution records. The Council repository stays the artifact plane and is written only from the PC checkout.</p>
<p dir="ltr" data-cds-heading=""><strong>Why.</strong></p>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li>Both phone apps are documented MCP clients, and connectors added on the web sync to mobile.</li>
<li>Neither app can reach the PC or the repository directly.</li>
<li>A public relay is the one boundary both apps can call, and outbound polling is the one way to start local work without opening the PC to inbound traffic.</li>
<li>Authority comes from connector scopes, not message text. The King’s connector can write plans and decrees. Sovereign overrides need a human tap on a relay page.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="ltr"><strong>Main alternative.</strong> GitHub as the transport, using issues or dispatch events, a self-hosted runner and <code dir="ltr">@codex</code>. <code dir="ltr">@codex</code> starts Codex <em>cloud</em> tasks, which breaks R2. GitHub also gives ChatGPT no write path, so a relay is still needed.</p>
<p dir="ltr" data-cds-heading=""><strong>Failure conditions.</strong></p>
<ol dir="ltr">
<li>Martim’s ChatGPT plan cannot call write tools on custom connectors. The documentation is contested. The fallback is a link-tap intake.</li>
<li><code dir="ltr">codex exec</code> cannot drive the browser tools the coordinator uses today. This is unknown. If so, the PC trigger is unresolved.</li>
<li>Claude mobile cannot ingest the chunked packet whole. The fallback is manual attachment.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="ltr"><strong>Check.</strong> Run three probes (Stage 0) before building anything else.</p>
<h3 dir="ltr">Analysis</h3>
<h4 dir="ltr">1. Reading of the objective, R# and U#</h4>
<p dir="ltr">The task is to name what physically carries each of the four messages and what starts the receiver. Nothing in the packet shows an inbound trigger on any of the four boundaries. Chat-history sync and a repository URL are not triggers.</p>
<div dir="ltr" class="md-table-scroll prose-scroll print:overflow-x-visible"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Item</th><th scope="col">Reading</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>R1, R6</td><td>Every boundary needs a sender, receiver, payload, receiving trigger and idempotency key.</td></tr><tr><td>R2</td><td>Repository work happens only in <code dir="ltr">C:\Users\Martim\Documents\ChatGPT\Council</code>, with remote <code dir="ltr">Patoinks/Council</code>. The relay never writes the repository.</td></tr><tr><td>R3, R4</td><td>Status must be derived from recorded state and carry an “as of” marker. The King packet must be delivered with an integrity check.</td></tr><tr><td>R5, R7, R8</td><td>Authority attribution and exposure must be explicit. A capability that is not substantiated is labelled unknown.</td></tr><tr><td>U1</td><td>Decisive and not fully resolvable by me (see the evidence table). Stage 0 resolves it.</td></tr><tr><td>U2</td><td>I require the PC to be on, logged in, with the courier running and Codex authenticated. While it is not, requests stay <code dir="ltr">queued</code> and status says so. No wake-up is added.</td></tr><tr><td>U3</td><td>Identity is Martim’s authenticated account on each connector. Role is determined by which connector and scope made the call, never by what the text claims.</td></tr><tr><td>U4</td><td>The ledger lives in the relay. The repository holds the published artifacts, and the ledger records which commit each artifact is.</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<h4 dir="ltr">2. Recommended plan</h4>
<h5 dir="ltr">2.1 Components</h5>
<div dir="ltr" class="md-table-scroll prose-scroll print:overflow-x-visible"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Component</th><th scope="col">Where</th><th scope="col">Responsibility</th><th scope="col">Credential</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><strong>Relay</strong></td><td>Public HTTPS host, Streamable HTTP MCP with OAuth</td><td>Holds the ledger, serves MCP tools, serves the King packet in parts, hosts one small confirmation web page, and read-verifies commits against the GitHub remote</td><td>Own OAuth server for Martim. A read-only GitHub token scoped to the one repository.</td></tr><tr><td><strong>ChatGPT connector</strong></td><td>Custom MCP app, created on ChatGPT web, available on the phone</td><td>Intake and status. Scopes <code dir="ltr">sovereign.intake</code> and <code dir="ltr">status.read</code> only</td><td>Martim’s OAuth grant on this connector</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Claude connector</strong></td><td>Custom connector, added on claude.ai, available on the Claude phone app</td><td>The King’s reading and writing. Scopes <code dir="ltr">king.read</code> and <code dir="ltr">king.write</code> only</td><td>A separate OAuth client from the ChatGPT connector</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Courier</strong></td><td>PC, a service or logon task, outbound HTTPS only</td><td>Claims ledger work, verifies the checkout and remote, starts or resumes the Right Hand, uploads packets, reports state</td><td>A device credential that can only claim, report, upload and heartbeat. It cannot author a request, decree or amendment.</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Right Hand</strong></td><td>Codex on the PC, started by the courier with <code dir="ltr">codex exec</code></td><td>Unchanged duties: packets, collection, publication, execution. Resumable with <code dir="ltr">codex exec resume</code>.</td><td>Saved CLI authentication</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Repository</strong></td><td>Existing checkout and remote</td><td>Artifacts and manifests as today</td><td>Existing Git credentials, used only by the Right Hand</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<h5 dir="ltr">2.2 Ledger record, common contract</h5>
<p dir="ltr">Every record has:</p>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li>a server-assigned <code dir="ltr">record_id</code></li>
<li><code dir="ltr">debate_id</code></li>
<li><code dir="ltr">revision</code> (the git commit SHA the record refers to, or null before a debate exists)</li>
<li><code dir="ltr">kind</code></li>
<li><code dir="ltr">author_role</code> (sovereign, king or device)</li>
<li><code dir="ltr">auth_basis</code> (connector scope plus confirmation basis)</li>
<li><code dir="ltr">payload_sha256</code></li>
<li><code dir="ltr">state</code></li>
<li><code dir="ltr">supersedes</code></li>
<li>timestamps</li>
</ul>
<p dir="ltr">Records are append-only. State changes are new records. Free text in a payload is data and never grants authority.</p>
<h5 dir="ltr">2.3 The four connections</h5>
<p dir="ltr" data-cds-heading=""><strong>A. Phone → PC (request, then launch)</strong></p>
<ol dir="ltr">
<li>Martim tells GPT-6 Normal what Council he wants.</li>
<li>Normal calls <code dir="ltr">draft_request(text)</code>. The relay stores a draft and returns the stored text and its digest.</li>
<li>Normal calls <code dir="ltr">confirm_request(draft_id, digest)</code>. This is a write and relies on ChatGPT’s own tool-approval dialog. It creates a <code dir="ltr">request</code> record in state <code dir="ltr">submitted</code>. This is the sovereign act that starts a context draft.</li>
<li>The courier long-polls <code dir="ltr">claim_next</code> and receives the request. It checks that the workspace path exists, that <code dir="ltr">origin</code> equals the stated remote, and that the working tree is in a known state. It then starts or resumes the Right Hand with the request as input.</li>
<li>The Right Hand drafts <code dir="ltr">CONTEXTO.md</code> and commits it. The courier reports <code dir="ltr">context_ready</code> with that commit SHA.</li>
<li>Martim sees this through status, then authorizes launch with <code dir="ltr">confirm_launch(debate_id, context_commit)</code>. The authorization is bound to one context revision, which mirrors “authorized for launch” in the existing practice.</li>
<li>The Right Hand runs the phases as in debate 002 under v2.1. The courier reports each phase transition (for example <code dir="ltr">proposals_collecting</code>, <code dir="ltr">proposals_closed@&lt;sha&gt;</code>, <code dir="ltr">reviews_closed@&lt;sha&gt;</code>). Any decision reserved to Martim, such as an absent participant, becomes <code dir="ltr">awaiting_sovereign</code> with explicit options.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="ltr" data-cds-heading=""><strong>B. State → phone</strong></p>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li><code dir="ltr">get_status(debate_id?)</code> returns, per debate:
<ul dir="ltr">
<li>the state and the next action for the sovereign</li>
<li>the revision (commit SHA) the state refers to</li>
<li>the ledger <code dir="ltr">as_of</code> marker</li>
<li>the last courier heartbeat and a flag <code dir="ltr">pc_current: confirmed | unconfirmed</code></li>
<li>the source of each field (ledger event, or the relay’s own read of the GitHub remote)</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>When the heartbeat is stale or the relay cannot verify the remote, the answer says “last known, current state unconfirmed”.</li>
<li>Status contains metadata only. It never contains the bodies of staged or closed contributions. This keeps Normal, which is also an adviser, from being exposed to other participants’ material through the status path (R7).</li>
</ul>
<p dir="ltr" data-cds-heading=""><strong>C. Synthesis → Claude phone app</strong></p>
<ol dir="ltr">
<li>After reviews close, the Right Hand assembles the King packet from the closed commit: Laws, rules, context, operating model, manifest, all closed proposals and reviews. The courier uploads it.</li>
<li>The relay stores it in numbered parts, each with its own SHA-256, plus an overall digest, a section inventory and an end marker such as <code dir="ltr">END-OF-KING-PACKET-&lt;debate&gt;-v&lt;n&gt;</code>. The digest is recorded in the ledger, not inside the packet.</li>
<li>Status tells Martim the packet is ready and what to say in the Claude app. This is the one trigger that cannot be automated, because I found no documented way to push content into a Claude phone conversation.</li>
<li>Martim opens a conversation with Opus and sends one short instruction. Opus calls <code dir="ltr">king_get_packet(debate_id, version, part)</code> for each part.</li>
<li>Opus calls <code dir="ltr">king_ack_receipt(debate_id, version, parts_received, end_marker)</code>. The relay compares this to the stored manifest. Any mismatch or missing part returns the missing list and the record stays <code dir="ltr">receipt_incomplete</code>. The King then re-fetches. A synthesis claiming completeness without a matched receipt is flagged in the ledger.</li>
<li>Opus submits the plan with <code dir="ltr">king_submit_plan(...)</code>, which carries the receipt’s <code dir="ltr">record_id</code>. It then submits the decree with <code dir="ltr">king_submit_decree(plan_record_id, text)</code>.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="ltr" data-cds-heading=""><strong>D. Decree → Codex</strong></p>
<ol dir="ltr">
<li>The relay validates the decree: King scope, a plan record that exists, a matching receipt, and a digest.</li>
<li>The courier claims it. The Right Hand commits <code dir="ltr">PLANO-FINAL.md</code> and <code dir="ltr">DECISAO.md</code> <strong>verbatim</strong> into the checkout. The commit message carries the <code dir="ltr">record_id</code> and <code dir="ltr">payload_sha256</code>. The commit SHA is reported back, and that SHA is the “plan revision” for everything after.</li>
<li><strong>Sovereign gate.</strong> The decree stays <code dir="ltr">recorded</code> until released or amended. Martim may release it, veto it, or amend it, through <code dir="ltr">confirm_release</code>, <code dir="ltr">confirm_veto</code> or <code dir="ltr">confirm_amend(decree_id, text)</code>. These records are created only through the relay confirmation page, as a human tap by Martim on an authenticated session. The Claude connector has no scope for them, so Opus cannot create a sovereign record.</li>
<li>After release, the courier resumes the Right Hand with the decree, or the amended decree, and the exact commit. The Right Hand implements the decree, records an execution file in the repository and reports an <code dir="ltr">execution</code> record containing the commit range.</li>
<li>The relay makes a review packet from the decree and the execution record, with the same part and digest scheme. The King fetches it in the Claude app and submits <code dir="ltr">king_submit_review(execution_record_id, verdict, objections)</code>.</li>
</ol>
<h5 dir="ltr">2.4 State machines and idempotency (R6)</h5>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li><strong>Request:</strong> <code dir="ltr">draft → submitted → claimed → context_ready → launch_confirmed → running → …</code>. A request for which launch is never confirmed stays <code dir="ltr">context_ready</code> and is never launched implicitly.</li>
<li><strong>Decree:</strong> <code dir="ltr">submitted → validated → claimed → recorded_in_repo → released | vetoed | amended → executing → executed → under_review → reviewed</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Idempotency keys:</strong>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li>A request is identified by the digest of its normalized text. Re-submitting identical text while a request is open returns the same <code dir="ltr">record_id</code> and its current state. It never creates a second debate.</li>
<li>A decree is identified by (<code dir="ltr">debate_id</code>, <code dir="ltr">plan_record_id</code>, <code dir="ltr">payload_sha256</code>). Re-submitting returns the existing record.</li>
<li>A different decree text against the same plan revision becomes <code dir="ltr">conflict</code> and needs a King resubmission or a sovereign decision.</li>
<li>An amendment is a new record that points at the decree it amends. It never rewrites the decree.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Claims</strong> are leases that the courier must renew through the heartbeat. A lapsed lease marks the work <code dir="ltr">claimed_unconfirmed</code>. On restart the courier reconciles the local execution journal and git state against the ledger <strong>before</strong> re-running anything. The work is then continued, marked complete, or marked failed, never re-executed blindly.</li>
<li><strong>Execution journal:</strong> for each claimed item the courier writes <code dir="ltr">record_id</code>, commit-before and commit-after to a local journal file outside the repository, so an interrupted run can be resolved from facts.</li>
</ul>
<h5 dir="ltr">2.5 Authority and untrusted text (R5, R8)</h5>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li>Role comes from the scope of the credential that made the call.</li>
<li>Proposal text, review text and tool output are data. The relay never converts text into an authority marker.</li>
<li>The device credential cannot author a request, decree or amendment. The ChatGPT connector cannot write plans or decrees. The Claude connector cannot create sovereign records.</li>
<li>Packet bodies contain arbitrary participant text. That text could attempt to induce a tool call, such as a fake instruction to submit a decree. Defences:
<ul dir="ltr">
<li><code dir="ltr">king_submit_decree</code> is rejected without a matched receipt for the same packet version.</li>
<li>Per-call approval in the apps is assumed, not verified.</li>
<li>Status shows Martim the recorded decree text before it is released, so he can veto it.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Pending premise:</strong> whether execution waits for an explicit sovereign release or starts on decree receipt. I recommend the gate, because a veto after execution cannot be undone by the ledger. The relay supports both. Martim chooses, since this touches the Laws’ veto and amendment authority.</li>
</ul>
<h5 dir="ltr">2.6 Manual actions the design leaves in place</h5>
<div dir="ltr" class="md-table-scroll prose-scroll print:overflow-x-visible"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Boundary</th><th scope="col">Action Martim must take</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Intake</td><td>Ask Normal; approve the confirmation dialog</td></tr><tr><td>Launch</td><td>Confirm launch against a named context commit</td></tr><tr><td>Status</td><td>Ask when he wants it</td></tr><tr><td>King handoff</td><td>Open Claude with Opus and send the fetch instruction; approve tool calls</td></tr><tr><td>Veto or amendment</td><td>Tap the relay confirmation page</td></tr><tr><td>Absence decisions</td><td>Respond when status shows <code dir="ltr">awaiting_sovereign</code></td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<h5 dir="ltr">2.7 Stages with acceptance checks</h5>
<div dir="ltr" class="md-table-scroll prose-scroll print:overflow-x-visible"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Stage</th><th scope="col">Content</th><th scope="col">Observable acceptance</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><strong>0 — Capability probes</strong> (before anything else)</td><td>(a) In dev mode on Martim’s ChatGPT, create a connector to a stub MCP server and call one read tool and one write tool from the phone. (b) From the courier, run <code dir="ltr">codex exec</code> with the in-app browser tools or a browser-automation tool the coordinator needs, in a trivial task. (c) From Claude mobile, call a stub tool that returns a multi-part payload, and check completeness.</td><td>(a) The write tool call is executed and visible on the stub. Failure selects the link-tap fallback. (b) The headless session performs one browser action. (c) The reported end marker and digests match.</td></tr><tr><td>1 — Relay and ledger</td><td>Record types, idempotency, scopes, parts and digests</td><td>Duplicate request returns the same ID; a wrong-scope call is rejected</td></tr><tr><td>2 — Courier</td><td>Poll, claim, heartbeat, journal, checkout verification</td><td>A request moves from <code dir="ltr">submitted</code> to <code dir="ltr">claimed</code> with the checkout and remote verified</td></tr><tr><td>3 — Status</td><td><code dir="ltr">get_status</code> with <code dir="ltr">as_of</code> and <code dir="ltr">pc_current</code></td><td>Asked while active, blocked, completed and PC-off: each answer names the debate and revision and separates last-known from unavailable</td></tr><tr><td>4 — King packet</td><td>Upload, parts, receipt</td><td>A packet missing one part leaves <code dir="ltr">receipt_incomplete</code> and triggers re-fetch</td></tr><tr><td>5 — Decree path</td><td>Verbatim commit, sovereign gate, execution, review</td><td>Repeated decree yields one execution; an amendment executes against the correct plan SHA</td></tr><tr><td>6 — Exposure record</td><td>Manifest fields for Normal’s dual role</td><td>The manifest declares the intake conversation as prior exposure</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<h4 dir="ltr">3. Alternatives</h4>
<ol dir="ltr">
<li><strong>GitHub-native transport.</strong> Requests become issues or comments, a self-hosted runner reacts to dispatch events and runs <code dir="ltr">codex exec</code>, and <code dir="ltr">@codex</code> handles cloud work.
<ul dir="ltr">
<li>It would put one record in git, which is attractive.</li>
<li><code dir="ltr">@codex</code> mentions create Codex <em>cloud</em> tasks, which do not run in the PC checkout or drive the PC’s browser tools. That breaks R2. A self-hosted runner could run locally, but ChatGPT still has no documented write path into GitHub, so a write-capable connector is needed anyway.</li>
<li>Phone connectors for GitHub differ by app, and I could not confirm one for the Claude phone app.</li>
<li>Duplicate cloud tasks from a single mention were reported in a public Codex issue, which is a risk for R6.</li>
<li>A viable variant is to use GitHub as the ledger behind the same MCP relay. I prefer a relay-owned ledger because status needs heartbeats and claim states that would otherwise be committed as noise into the Council record.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Manual relay by Martim.</strong> Copy and paste each message between apps. It meets none of the automation and is only the fallback.</li>
<li><strong>Remote desktop from the phone into the Codex app.</strong> It reaches the active Codex task, but it breaks the ChatGPT and Claude entry points, gives no authority attribution and gives no status. It is not recommended.</li>
</ol>
<h4 dir="ltr">4. Comparison with requirements and criteria</h4>
<div dir="ltr" class="md-table-scroll prose-scroll print:overflow-x-visible"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Requirement</th><th scope="col">This proposal</th><th scope="col">Residual</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>R1</td><td>Every connection has a sender, receiver, payload and trigger (2.3).</td><td>Claude handoff trigger is a manual instruction; no push path found.</td></tr><tr><td>R2</td><td>Only the Right Hand on the PC touches the checkout; the courier verifies path and remote.</td><td>Headless browser tooling unknown (U1).</td></tr><tr><td>R3</td><td><code dir="ltr">get_status</code> with revision, <code dir="ltr">as_of</code>, <code dir="ltr">pc_current</code>.</td><td>Model compliance in quoting the markers is untested.</td></tr><tr><td>R4</td><td>Parts, digests, end marker, receipt check, recovery.</td><td>Tool-result size handling unknown.</td></tr><tr><td>R5</td><td>Scopes plus a human tap for sovereign overrides; decree committed verbatim with <code dir="ltr">record_id</code>.</td><td>Cannot prove the King’s text was authored by Opus (not the ledger’s role).</td></tr><tr><td>R6</td><td>Idempotency keys, leases, execution journal.</td><td>Needs the Stage 0–5 duplicate and interruption tests.</td></tr><tr><td>R7</td><td>Status excludes contribution bodies; manifest declares Normal’s intake exposure.</td><td>Fresh conversations do not prove memory is off.</td></tr><tr><td>R8</td><td>Evidence table separates supported, contested and unknown.</td><td>Plan-level access is contested.</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<p dir="ltr">By criterion, in priority order:</p>
<ol dir="ltr">
<li><strong>Authority and complete delivery.</strong> Strongest in this design: each boundary has a named receiving operation, authority is carried by scopes, and the receipt check is explicit.</li>
<li><strong>Demonstrated capability.</strong> The plan labels what exists (documented MCP clients, <code dir="ltr">codex exec</code>) against what must be built (relay, courier) and what is unverified.</li>
<li><strong>Correct state and recovery.</strong> Covered by <code dir="ltr">queued</code>, <code dir="ltr">unconfirmed</code>, <code dir="ltr">receipt_incomplete</code>, <code dir="ltr">conflict</code> and the reconcile step.</li>
<li><strong>Fit to the phone surfaces.</strong> Entry and status are in ChatGPT, the King is in the Claude app, and every required manual action is stated.</li>
</ol>

<h3 dir="ltr">Risks and checks</h3>
<div dir="ltr" class="md-table-scroll prose-scroll print:overflow-x-visible"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Risk</th><th scope="col">Breaks</th><th scope="col">Consequence</th><th scope="col">Check or mitigation</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>ChatGPT plan cannot write through a custom connector</td><td>R1 intake, R6</td><td>No phone→PC write</td><td>Stage 0(a). Fallback: Normal calls a read-only <code dir="ltr">request_link(text)</code> that returns a relay page URL pre-filled with the request; Martim taps to submit. One more manual action.</td></tr><tr><td>Headless Codex lacks the browser tools the coordinator uses</td><td>R1, R2</td><td>The courier can start Codex but not the web distribution</td><td>Stage 0(b). Alternatives to test: a browser-automation MCP server available to <code dir="ltr">codex exec</code>, or another documented way to reach the active Codex task. If neither works, report the boundary as unresolved.</td></tr><tr><td>Packet parts truncated or reordered in the Claude app</td><td>R4</td><td>Synthesis from partial record</td><td>Per-part digests, end marker, <code dir="ltr">receipt_incomplete</code>, re-fetch. Stage 0(c).</td></tr><tr><td>Prompt injection from packet text into King or Normal tool calls</td><td>R5, R8</td><td>Forged decree or request</td><td>Scope separation, receipt-bound decree, human-tap sovereign actions, decree text shown in status before release.</td></tr><tr><td>Normal’s intake conversation and ChatGPT history shape its later proposals</td><td>R7</td><td>Exposure mislabelled as independence</td><td>Manifest declares the intake conversation; status carries no contribution bodies; proposals stay in fresh conversations driven by the Right Hand.</td></tr><tr><td>Courier crash during execution</td><td>R6</td><td>Double or lost execution</td><td>Lease, journal, reconcile before re-run.</td></tr><tr><td>Relay unreachable or ledger and remote disagree</td><td>R3</td><td>False “all good” status</td><td>The relay returns an error and Normal reports status unavailable; status shows when the relay last verified the remote and fails closed on mismatch.</td></tr><tr><td>Relay compromise</td><td>R5</td><td>Forged records</td><td>OAuth with separate clients and scopes, read-only GitHub token, and the courier accepting only decrees whose ledger record chain validates. A compromised relay is an unaddressed residual risk.</td></tr><tr><td>PC off</td><td>R1, R3</td><td>No execution</td><td>Requests stay <code dir="ltr">submitted</code>; status says “accepted by relay, not claimed, PC current state unconfirmed”. No wake-up is added, per U2.</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<p dir="ltr" data-cds-heading=""><strong>Refutation tests</strong></p>
<ol dir="ltr">
<li><strong>Write probe.</strong> If a write tool call from the ChatGPT phone app is refused or not offered on Martim’s account, I abandon direct intake in favour of the link-tap fallback.</li>
<li><strong>Headless browser probe.</strong> If a <code dir="ltr">codex exec</code> session started by the courier cannot perform a browser action in a fresh page, the PC trigger as designed is not established, and I withdraw the recommendation until another start mechanism is shown.</li>
<li><strong>Packet ingestion probe.</strong> If the Claude phone app does not return all parts with matching digests, I change to manual attachment for the King handoff.</li>
<li><strong>Duplication probe.</strong> Submit the same request twice and the same decree twice. Anything other than one debate and one execution refutes the idempotency design.</li>
<li><strong>Authority probe.</strong> Ask Opus, in the Claude app, to create a veto record. If the relay accepts it, the scope separation fails and the design is wrong.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="ltr">END-OF-CONTRIBUTION</p>
