## capturas/sonnet-rendered.html

<div data-perf-reply-text="" class="_blocks_4za3l_47 standard-markdown grid-cols-1 grid [&amp;_&gt;_*]:min-w-0 whitespace-normal break-words print:block"><p dir="ltr">END-OF-PACKET-003-PROPOSAL-v1 | Missing sections: none</p>
<h2 dir="ltr">Proposal — sonnet</h2>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li><strong>Participant:</strong> sonnet</li>
<li><strong>Visible model:</strong> Sonnet 5.5, taken from the session configuration. The interface label is not visible to me and is not independently attested.</li>
<li><strong>Date:</strong> 2026-10-17</li>
<li><strong>Phase and round:</strong> Proposals, round 01</li>
<li><strong>Context version:</strong> v1 (debate 003-mobile-bridge)</li>
<li><strong>Reference commit:</strong> source baseline 95d853ba7480260d5a9c4b8541b4b1b32a6d90f3; governance 389a4367de088361adcaeec271fb438c6fb0b492</li>
<li><strong>Files received and read:</strong> all seven sections, read in full: LEIS, REGRAS, CONTEXTO, OPERATING-MODEL, MANIFESTO, CONTRIBUICAO template, fixed phase prompt. None partial.</li>
<li><strong>Tools used:</strong> WebSearch (standard mode), six queries on ChatGPT custom MCP connectors, Claude remote MCP and mobile, Codex GitHub triggers, <code dir="ltr">codex exec</code>, GitHub self-hosted runners, and Claude/GitHub connectors. Only search-result excerpts were read; no page was fetched in full. Several excerpts came from third-party mirrors, noted in the evidence table.</li>
<li><strong>Cross-conversation memory:</strong> account-level memory exists in this deployment. Nothing in it concerns this debate and I did not use it.</li>
<li><strong>Prior exposure:</strong> none beyond this packet.</li>
<li><strong>New conversation:</strong> yes, as far as I can observe. The packet and routing line were the first content.</li>
<li><strong>Access limits:</strong> I cannot test Martim’s ChatGPT or Claude accounts, plans, phones or PC. Every capability claim is about documentation, not Martim’s setup.</li>
</ul>
<h3 dir="ltr">Brief — up to 300 words</h3>
<p dir="ltr"><strong>Recommendation.</strong> Build one small public HTTPS MCP server, the <strong>relay</strong>, with an append-only ledger. Attach it as a custom connector to both phone apps: ChatGPT for intake and status, Claude for the King. Add an outbound-only <strong>courier</strong> on the PC. The courier claims work from the relay and starts the existing Right Hand with <code dir="ltr">codex exec</code>. The relay is the control plane for requests, state, packet parts, decrees and execution records. The Council repository stays the artifact plane and is written only from the PC checkout.</p>
<p dir="ltr" data-cds-heading=""><strong>Why.</strong></p>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li>Both phone apps are documented MCP clients, and connectors added on the web sync to mobile.</li>
<li>Neither app can reach the PC or the repository directly.</li>
<li>A public relay is the one boundary both apps can call, and outbound polling is the one way to start local work without opening the PC to inbound traffic.</li>
<li>Authority comes from connector scopes, not message text. The King’s connector can write plans and decrees. Sovereign overrides need a human tap on a relay page.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="ltr"><strong>Main alternative.</strong> GitHub as the transport, using issues or dispatch events, a self-hosted runner and <code dir="ltr">@codex</code>. <code dir="ltr">@codex</code> starts Codex <em>cloud</em> tasks, which breaks R2. GitHub also gives ChatGPT no write path, so a relay is still needed.</p>
<p dir="ltr" data-cds-heading=""><strong>Failure conditions.</strong></p>
<ol dir="ltr">
<li>Martim’s ChatGPT plan cannot call write tools on custom connectors. The documentation is contested. The fallback is a link-tap intake.</li>
<li><code dir="ltr">codex exec</code> cannot drive the browser tools the coordinator uses today. This is unknown. If so, the PC trigger is unresolved.</li>
<li>Claude mobile cannot ingest the chunked packet whole. The fallback is manual attachment.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="ltr"><strong>Check.</strong> Run three probes (Stage 0) before building anything else.</p>
<h3 dir="ltr">Analysis</h3>
<h4 dir="ltr">1. Reading of the objective, R# and U#</h4>
<p dir="ltr">The task is to name what physically carries each of the four messages and what starts the receiver. Nothing in the packet shows an inbound trigger on any of the four boundaries. Chat-history sync and a repository URL are not triggers.</p>
<div dir="ltr" class="md-table-scroll prose-scroll print:overflow-x-visible"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col" style="">Item</th><th scope="col" style="">Reading</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>R1, R6</td><td>Every boundary needs a sender, receiver, payload, receiving trigger and idempotency key.</td></tr><tr><td>R2</td><td>Repository work happens only in <code dir="ltr">C:\Users\Martim\Documents\ChatGPT\Council</code>, with remote <code dir="ltr">Patoinks/Council</code>. The relay never writes the repository.</td></tr><tr><td>R3, R4</td><td>Status must be derived from recorded state and carry an “as of” marker. The King packet must be delivered with an integrity check.</td></tr><tr><td>R5, R7, R8</td><td>Authority attribution and exposure must be explicit. A capability that is not substantiated is labelled unknown.</td></tr><tr><td>U1</td><td>Decisive and not fully resolvable by me (see the evidence table). Stage 0 resolves it.</td></tr><tr><td>U2</td><td>I require the PC to be on, logged in, with the courier running and Codex authenticated. While it is not, requests stay <code dir="ltr">queued</code> and status says so. No wake-up is added.</td></tr><tr><td>U3</td><td>Identity is Martim’s authenticated account on each connector. Role is determined by which connector and scope made the call, never by what the text claims.</td></tr><tr><td>U4</td><td>The ledger lives in the relay. The repository holds the published artifacts, and the ledger records which commit each artifact is.</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<h4 dir="ltr">2. Recommended plan</h4>
<h5 dir="ltr">2.1 Components</h5>
<div dir="ltr" class="md-table-scroll prose-scroll print:overflow-x-visible"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col" style="">Component</th><th scope="col" style="">Where</th><th scope="col" style="">Responsibility</th><th scope="col" style="">Credential</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><strong>Relay</strong></td><td>Public HTTPS host, Streamable HTTP MCP with OAuth</td><td>Holds the ledger, serves MCP tools, serves the King packet in parts, hosts one small confirmation web page, and read-verifies commits against the GitHub remote</td><td>Own OAuth server for Martim. A read-only GitHub token scoped to the one repository.</td></tr><tr><td><strong>ChatGPT connector</strong></td><td>Custom MCP app, created on ChatGPT web, available on the phone</td><td>Intake and status. Scopes <code dir="ltr">sovereign.intake</code> and <code dir="ltr">status.read</code> only</td><td>Martim’s OAuth grant on this connector</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Claude connector</strong></td><td>Custom connector, added on claude.ai, available on the Claude phone app</td><td>The King’s reading and writing. Scopes <code dir="ltr">king.read</code> and <code dir="ltr">king.write</code> only</td><td>A separate OAuth client from the ChatGPT connector</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Courier</strong></td><td>PC, a service or logon task, outbound HTTPS only</td><td>Claims ledger work, verifies the checkout and remote, starts or resumes the Right Hand, uploads packets, reports state</td><td>A device credential that can only claim, report, upload and heartbeat. It cannot author a request, decree or amendment.</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Right Hand</strong></td><td>Codex on the PC, started by the courier with <code dir="ltr">codex exec</code></td><td>Unchanged duties: packets, collection, publication, execution. Resumable with <code dir="ltr">codex exec resume</code>.</td><td>Saved CLI authentication</td></tr><tr><td><strong>Repository</strong></td><td>Existing checkout and remote</td><td>Artifacts and manifests as today</td><td>Existing Git credentials, used only by the Right Hand</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<h5 dir="ltr">2.2 Ledger record, common contract</h5>
<p dir="ltr">Every record has:</p>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li>a server-assigned <code dir="ltr">record_id</code></li>
<li><code dir="ltr">debate_id</code></li>
<li><code dir="ltr">revision</code> (the git commit SHA the record refers to, or null before a debate exists)</li>
<li><code dir="ltr">kind</code></li>
<li><code dir="ltr">author_role</code> (sovereign, king or device)</li>
<li><code dir="ltr">auth_basis</code> (connector scope plus confirmation basis)</li>
<li><code dir="ltr">payload_sha256</code></li>
<li><code dir="ltr">state</code></li>
<li><code dir="ltr">supersedes</code></li>
<li>timestamps</li>
</ul>
<p dir="ltr">Records are append-only. State changes are new records. Free text in a payload is data and never grants authority.</p>
<h5 dir="ltr">2.3 The four connections</h5>
<p dir="ltr" data-cds-heading=""><strong>A. Phone → PC (request, then launch)</strong></p>
<ol dir="ltr">
<li>Martim tells GPT-6 Normal what Council he wants.</li>
<li>Normal calls <code dir="ltr">draft_request(text)</code>. The relay stores a draft and returns the stored text and its digest.</li>
<li>Normal calls <code dir="ltr">confirm_request(draft_id, digest)</code>. This is a write and relies on ChatGPT’s own tool-approval dialog. It creates a <code dir="ltr">request</code> record in state <code dir="ltr">submitted</code>. This is the sovereign act that starts a context draft.</li>
<li>The courier long-polls <code dir="ltr">claim_next</code> and receives the request. It checks that the workspace path exists, that <code dir="ltr">origin</code> equals the stated remote, and that the working tree is in a known state. It then starts or resumes the Right Hand with the request as input.</li>
<li>The Right Hand drafts <code dir="ltr">CONTEXTO.md</code> and commits it. The courier reports <code dir="ltr">context_ready</code> with that commit SHA.</li>
<li>Martim sees this through status, then authorizes launch with <code dir="ltr">confirm_launch(debate_id, context_commit)</code>. The authorization is bound to one context revision, which mirrors “authorized for launch” in the existing practice.</li>
<li>The Right Hand runs the phases as in debate 002 under v2.1. The courier reports each phase transition (for example <code dir="ltr">proposals_collecting</code>, <code dir="ltr">proposals_closed@&lt;sha&gt;</code>, <code dir="ltr">reviews_closed@&lt;sha&gt;</code>). Any decision reserved to Martim, such as an absent participant, becomes <code dir="ltr">awaiting_sovereign</code> with explicit options.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="ltr" data-cds-heading=""><strong>B. State → phone</strong></p>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li><code dir="ltr">get_status(debate_id?)</code> returns, per debate:
<ul dir="ltr">
<li>the state and the next action for the sovereign</li>
<li>the revision (commit SHA) the state refers to</li>
<li>the ledger <code dir="ltr">as_of</code> marker</li>
<li>the last courier heartbeat and a flag <code dir="ltr">pc_current: confirmed | unconfirmed</code></li>
<li>the source of each field (ledger event, or the relay’s own read of the GitHub remote)</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>When the heartbeat is stale or the relay cannot verify the remote, the answer says “last known, current state unconfirmed”.</li>
<li>Status contains metadata only. It never contains the bodies of staged or closed contributions. This keeps Normal, which is also an adviser, from being exposed to other participants’ material through the status path (R7).</li>
</ul>
<p dir="ltr" data-cds-heading=""><strong>C. Synthesis → Claude phone app</strong></p>
<ol dir="ltr">
<li>After reviews close, the Right Hand assembles the King packet from the closed commit: Laws, rules, context, operating model, manifest, all closed proposals and reviews. The courier uploads it.</li>
<li>The relay stores it in numbered parts, each with its own SHA-256, plus an overall digest, a section inventory and an end marker such as <code dir="ltr">END-OF-KING-PACKET-&lt;debate&gt;-v&lt;n&gt;</code>. The digest is recorded in the ledger, not inside the packet.</li>
<li>Status tells Martim the packet is ready and what to say in the Claude app. This is the one trigger that cannot be automated, because I found no documented way to push content into a Claude phone conversation.</li>
<li>Martim opens a conversation with Opus and sends one short instruction. Opus calls <code dir="ltr">king_get_packet(debate_id, version, part)</code> for each part.</li>
<li>Opus calls <code dir="ltr">king_ack_receipt(debate_id, version, parts_received, end_marker)</code>. The relay compares this to the stored manifest. Any mismatch or missing part returns the missing list and the record stays <code dir="ltr">receipt_incomplete</code>. The King then re-fetches. A synthesis claiming completeness without a matched receipt is flagged in the ledger.</li>
<li>Opus submits the plan with <code dir="ltr">king_submit_plan(...)</code>, which carries the receipt’s <code dir="ltr">record_id</code>. It then submits the decree with <code dir="ltr">king_submit_decree(plan_record_id, text)</code>.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="ltr" data-cds-heading=""><strong>D. Decree → Codex</strong></p>
<ol dir="ltr">
<li>The relay validates the decree: King scope, a plan record that exists, a matching receipt, and a digest.</li>
<li>The courier claims it. The Right Hand commits <code dir="ltr">PLANO-FINAL.md</code> and <code dir="ltr">DECISAO.md</code> <strong>verbatim</strong> into the checkout. The commit message carries the <code dir="ltr">record_id</code> and <code dir="ltr">payload_sha256</code>. The commit SHA is reported back, and that SHA is the “plan revision” for everything after.</li>
<li><strong>Sovereign gate.</strong> The decree stays <code dir="ltr">recorded</code> until released or amended. Martim may release it, veto it, or amend it, through <code dir="ltr">confirm_release</code>, <code dir="ltr">confirm_veto</code> or <code dir="ltr">confirm_amend(decree_id, text)</code>. These records are created only through the relay confirmation page, as a human tap by Martim on an authenticated session. The Claude connector has no scope for them, so Opus cannot create a sovereign record.</li>
<li>After release, the courier resumes the Right Hand with the decree, or the amended decree, and the exact commit. The Right Hand implements the decree, records an execution file in the repository and reports an <code dir="ltr">execution</code> record containing the commit range.</li>
<li>The relay makes a review packet from the decree and the execution record, with the same part and digest scheme. The King fetches it in the Claude app and submits <code dir="ltr">king_submit_review(execution_record_id, verdict, objections)</code>.</li>
</ol>
<h5 dir="ltr">2.4 State machines and idempotency (R6)</h5>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li><strong>Request:</strong> <code dir="ltr">draft → submitted → claimed → context_ready → launch_confirmed → running → …</code>. A request for which launch is never confirmed stays <code dir="ltr">context_ready</code> and is never launched implicitly.</li>
<li><strong>Decree:</strong> <code dir="ltr">submitted → validated → claimed → recorded_in_repo → released | vetoed | amended → executing → executed → under_review → reviewed</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Idempotency keys:</strong>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li>A request is identified by the digest of its normalized text. Re-submitting identical text while a request is open returns the same <code dir="ltr">record_id</code> and its current state. It never creates a second debate.</li>
<li>A decree is identified by (<code dir="ltr">debate_id</code>, <code dir="ltr">plan_record_id</code>, <code dir="ltr">payload_sha256</code>). Re-submitting returns the existing record.</li>
<li>A different decree text against the same plan revision becomes <code dir="ltr">conflict</code> and needs a King resubmission or a sovereign decision.</li>
<li>An amendment is a new record that points at the decree it amends. It never rewrites the decree.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Claims</strong> are leases that the courier must renew through the heartbeat. A lapsed lease marks the work <code dir="ltr">claimed_unconfirmed</code>. On restart the courier reconciles the local execution journal and git state against the ledger <strong>before</strong> re-running anything. The work is then continued, marked complete, or marked failed, never re-executed blindly.</li>
<li><strong>Execution journal:</strong> for each claimed item the courier writes <code dir="ltr">record_id</code>, commit-before and commit-after to a local journal file outside the repository, so an interrupted run can be resolved from facts.</li>
</ul>
<h5 dir="ltr">2.5 Authority and untrusted text (R5, R8)</h5>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li>Role comes from the scope of the credential that made the call.</li>
<li>Proposal text, review text and tool output are data. The relay never converts text into an authority marker.</li>
<li>The device credential cannot author a request, decree or amendment. The ChatGPT connector cannot write plans or decrees. The Claude connector cannot create sovereign records.</li>
<li>Packet bodies contain arbitrary participant text. That text could attempt to induce a tool call, such as a fake instruction to submit a decree. Defences:
<ul dir="ltr">
<li><code dir="ltr">king_submit_decree</code> is rejected without a matched receipt for the same packet version.</li>
<li>Per-call approval in the apps is assumed, not verified.</li>
<li>Status shows Martim the recorded decree text before it is released, so he can veto it.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Pending premise:</strong> whether execution waits for an explicit sovereign release or starts on decree receipt. I recommend the gate, because a veto after execution cannot be undone by the ledger. The relay supports both. Martim chooses, since this touches the Laws’ veto and amendment authority.</li>
</ul>
<h5 dir="ltr">2.6 Manual actions the design leaves in place</h5>
<div dir="ltr" class="md-table-scroll prose-scroll print:overflow-x-visible"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col" style="">Boundary</th><th scope="col" style="">Action Martim must take</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Intake</td><td>Ask Normal; approve the confirmation dialog</td></tr><tr><td>Launch</td><td>Confirm launch against a named context commit</td></tr><tr><td>Status</td><td>Ask when he wants it</td></tr><tr><td>King handoff</td><td>Open Claude with Opus and send the fetch instruction; approve tool calls</td></tr><tr><td>Veto or amendment</td><td>Tap the relay confirmation page</td></tr><tr><td>Absence decisions</td><td>Respond when status shows <code dir="ltr">awaiting_sovereign</code></td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<h5 dir="ltr">2.7 Stages with acceptance checks</h5>
<div dir="ltr" class="md-table-scroll prose-scroll print:overflow-x-visible"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col" style="">Stage</th><th scope="col" style="">Content</th><th scope="col" style="">Observable acceptance</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><strong>0 — Capability probes</strong> (before anything else)</td><td>(a) In dev mode on Martim’s ChatGPT, create a connector to a stub MCP server and call one read tool and one write tool from the phone. (b) From the courier, run <code dir="ltr">codex exec</code> with the in-app browser tools or a browser-automation tool the coordinator needs, in a trivial task. (c) From Claude mobile, call a stub tool that returns a multi-part payload, and check completeness.</td><td>(a) The write tool call is executed and visible on the stub. Failure selects the link-tap fallback. (b) The headless session performs one browser action. (c) The reported end marker and digests match.</td></tr><tr><td>1 — Relay and ledger</td><td>Record types, idempotency, scopes, parts and digests</td><td>Duplicate request returns the same ID; a wrong-scope call is rejected</td></tr><tr><td>2 — Courier</td><td>Poll, claim, heartbeat, journal, checkout verification</td><td>A request moves from <code dir="ltr">submitted</code> to <code dir="ltr">claimed</code> with the checkout and remote verified</td></tr><tr><td>3 — Status</td><td><code dir="ltr">get_status</code> with <code dir="ltr">as_of</code> and <code dir="ltr">pc_current</code></td><td>Asked while active, blocked, completed and PC-off: each answer names the debate and revision and separates last-known from unavailable</td></tr><tr><td>4 — King packet</td><td>Upload, parts, receipt</td><td>A packet missing one part leaves <code dir="ltr">receipt_incomplete</code> and triggers re-fetch</td></tr><tr><td>5 — Decree path</td><td>Verbatim commit, sovereign gate, execution, review</td><td>Repeated decree yields one execution; an amendment executes against the correct plan SHA</td></tr><tr><td>6 — Exposure record</td><td>Manifest fields for Normal’s dual role</td><td>The manifest declares the intake conversation as prior exposure</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<h4 dir="ltr">3. Alternatives</h4>
<ol dir="ltr">
<li><strong>GitHub-native transport.</strong> Requests become issues or comments, a self-hosted runner reacts to dispatch events and runs <code dir="ltr">codex exec</code>, and <code dir="ltr">@codex</code> handles cloud work.
<ul dir="ltr">
<li>It would put one record in git, which is attractive.</li>
<li><code dir="ltr">@codex</code> mentions create Codex <em>cloud</em> tasks, which do not run in the PC checkout or drive the PC’s browser tools. That breaks R2. A self-hosted runner could run locally, but ChatGPT still has no documented write path into GitHub, so a write-capable connector is needed anyway.</li>
<li>Phone connectors for GitHub differ by app, and I could not confirm one for the Claude phone app.</li>
<li>Duplicate cloud tasks from a single mention were reported in a public Codex issue, which is a risk for R6.</li>
<li>A viable variant is to use GitHub as the ledger behind the same MCP relay. I prefer a relay-owned ledger because status needs heartbeats and claim states that would otherwise be committed as noise into the Council record.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Manual relay by Martim.</strong> Copy and paste each message between apps. It meets none of the automation and is only the fallback.</li>
<li><strong>Remote desktop from the phone into the Codex app.</strong> It reaches the active Codex task, but it breaks the ChatGPT and Claude entry points, gives no authority attribution and gives no status. It is not recommended.</li>
</ol>
<h4 dir="ltr">4. Comparison with requirements and criteria</h4>
<div dir="ltr" class="md-table-scroll prose-scroll print:overflow-x-visible"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col" style="">Requirement</th><th scope="col" style="">This proposal</th><th scope="col" style="">Residual</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>R1</td><td>Every connection has a sender, receiver, payload and trigger (2.3).</td><td>Claude handoff trigger is a manual instruction; no push path found.</td></tr><tr><td>R2</td><td>Only the Right Hand on the PC touches the checkout; the courier verifies path and remote.</td><td>Headless browser tooling unknown (U1).</td></tr><tr><td>R3</td><td><code dir="ltr">get_status</code> with revision, <code dir="ltr">as_of</code>, <code dir="ltr">pc_current</code>.</td><td>Model compliance in quoting the markers is untested.</td></tr><tr><td>R4</td><td>Parts, digests, end marker, receipt check, recovery.</td><td>Tool-result size handling unknown.</td></tr><tr><td>R5</td><td>Scopes plus a human tap for sovereign overrides; decree committed verbatim with <code dir="ltr">record_id</code>.</td><td>Cannot prove the King’s text was authored by Opus (not the ledger’s role).</td></tr><tr><td>R6</td><td>Idempotency keys, leases, execution journal.</td><td>Needs the Stage 0–5 duplicate and interruption tests.</td></tr><tr><td>R7</td><td>Status excludes contribution bodies; manifest declares Normal’s intake exposure.</td><td>Fresh conversations do not prove memory is off.</td></tr><tr><td>R8</td><td>Evidence table separates supported, contested and unknown.</td><td>Plan-level access is contested.</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<p dir="ltr">By criterion, in priority order:</p>
<ol dir="ltr">
<li><strong>Authority and complete delivery.</strong> Strongest in this design: each boundary has a named receiving operation, authority is carried by scopes, and the receipt check is explicit.</li>
<li><strong>Demonstrated capability.</strong> The plan labels what exists (documented MCP clients, <code dir="ltr">codex exec</code>) against what must be built (relay, courier) and what is unverified.</li>
<li><strong>Correct state and recovery.</strong> Covered by <code dir="ltr">queued</code>, <code dir="ltr">unconfirmed</code>, <code dir="ltr">receipt_incomplete</code>, <code dir="ltr">conflict</code> and the reconcile step.</li>
<li><strong>Fit to the phone surfaces.</strong> Entry and status are in ChatGPT, the King is in the Claude app, and every required manual action is stated.</li>
</ol>
<h3 dir="ltr">Evidence and assumptions</h3>
<div dir="ltr" class="md-table-scroll prose-scroll print:overflow-x-visible"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col" style="">Decisive claim</th><th scope="col" style="">State</th><th scope="col" style="">Provenance and passage</th><th scope="col" style="">Phase</th><th scope="col" style="">Scope</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>ChatGPT can add a custom MCP connector in developer mode, pointed at a public <code dir="ltr">/mcp</code> URL, and the connector then appears on the ChatGPT mobile apps</td><td>supported</td><td>OpenAI’s Apps SDK documentation describes creating a connector from a public MCP endpoint and says it becomes available on mobile once linked on web.</td><td>Proposal, search</td><td>Mechanism exists. Not tested on Martim’s account or phone.</td></tr><tr><td>Whether Plus or Pro accounts may call <em>write</em> tools on custom connectors</td><td>contested</td><td>One mirror of vendor documentation says Plus and Pro are limited to read/fetch-only custom connectors and full write support is for Business, Enterprise and Education. Another vendor page says developer mode on Plus and Pro supports read and write. A third-party troubleshooting page describes Pro as restricted to read and fetch as of mid-2026. The official OpenAI help page I retrieved was a non-English translation that names only Business, Enterprise and Edu for write support.</td><td>Proposal, search</td><td>Decisive for the intake write. Stage 0(a) resolves it.</td></tr><tr><td>Claude mobile supports remote MCP connectors that must be added from the web, not from the phone</td><td>supported</td><td>Anthropic’s support article says remote MCP is supported on Claude mobile and that new servers cannot be added from the mobile app.</td><td>Proposal, search</td><td>Documented. Not tested for Martim’s plan.</td></tr><tr><td>Claude connects to a custom connector from Anthropic’s cloud, so the relay must be publicly reachable</td><td>attributed</td><td>A vendor’s copy of the setup guidance says Claude connects from Anthropic’s cloud infrastructure and the server must be publicly reachable. Source is a mirror, not the primary page.</td><td>Proposal, search</td><td>Drives the public-relay design.</td></tr><tr><td>Claude supports OAuth and Streamable HTTP remote servers</td><td>supported</td><td>The support article lists both transports and both authless and OAuth servers.</td><td>Proposal, search</td><td>Supports the relay’s auth design.</td></tr><tr><td><code dir="ltr">codex exec</code> runs non-interactively, defaults to a read-only sandbox, can allow edits, reuses saved authentication and can resume a session</td><td>supported</td><td>OpenAI’s non-interactive mode documentation describes these behaviours.</td><td>Proposal, search</td><td>Mechanism exists. It does not show that a headless session has the coordinator’s browser tools.</td></tr><tr><td>A headless <code dir="ltr">codex exec</code> session has the in-app browser tools the coordinator uses to drive Gemini, ChatGPT and Claude web pages</td><td>unknown</td><td>No retrieved passage addresses it.</td><td>Proposal, search</td><td>Decisive for the PC trigger. Stage 0(b).</td></tr><tr><td><code dir="ltr">@codex</code> on GitHub starts a Codex cloud task using the pull request as context</td><td>supported</td><td>OpenAI’s Codex GitHub documentation describes cloud tasks started by mentions.</td><td>Proposal, search</td><td>Applies to cloud tasks, not the PC checkout.</td></tr><tr><td>A single GitHub mention has produced duplicate cloud tasks</td><td>attributed</td><td>A public Codex issue reports one review mention creating several duplicate tasks.</td><td>Proposal, search</td><td>One user report. Relevant to R6 for the GitHub alternative.</td></tr><tr><td>A GitHub self-hosted runner can run a workflow on the user’s own machine from <code dir="ltr">workflow_dispatch</code></td><td>attributed</td><td>Third-party tutorials describe dispatching a workflow to a self-hosted runner.</td><td>Proposal, search</td><td>Alternative only.</td></tr><tr><td>A first-party GitHub connector exists for the Claude chat apps</td><td>contested</td><td>A public issue says the chat apps have no GitHub connector. A third-party guide describes one.</td><td>Proposal, search</td><td>The design does not rely on it.</td></tr><tr><td>How much tool-result text the Claude and ChatGPT phone apps accept and pass to the model intact</td><td>unknown</td><td>No retrieved passage.</td><td>Proposal</td><td>Decides part size. Stage 0(c).</td></tr><tr><td>An external system can push content into a Claude phone conversation</td><td>unknown</td><td>None found.</td><td>Proposal</td><td>The design assumes it cannot and keeps a manual start.</td></tr><tr><td>Per-call approval dialogs in both apps appear on write calls and show the arguments</td><td>assumption</td><td>ChatGPT: a help page says ChatGPT asks for confirmation based on app permissions and action context (non-English page). Claude: no passage retrieved.</td><td>Proposal, search</td><td>Needed for intake and King writes. Verify in Stage 0.</td></tr><tr><td>An outbound-only courier avoids exposing the PC to inbound connections</td><td>assumption</td><td>Design reasoning, no source</td><td>Proposal</td><td>Depends on the courier opening only outbound HTTPS.</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<h3 dir="ltr">Risks and checks</h3>
<div dir="ltr" class="md-table-scroll prose-scroll print:overflow-x-visible"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col" style="">Risk</th><th scope="col" style="">Breaks</th><th scope="col" style="">Consequence</th><th scope="col" style="">Check or mitigation</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>ChatGPT plan cannot write through a custom connector</td><td>R1 intake, R6</td><td>No phone→PC write</td><td>Stage 0(a). Fallback: Normal calls a read-only <code dir="ltr">request_link(text)</code> that returns a relay page URL pre-filled with the request; Martim taps to submit. One more manual action.</td></tr><tr><td>Headless Codex lacks the browser tools the coordinator uses</td><td>R1, R2</td><td>The courier can start Codex but not the web distribution</td><td>Stage 0(b). Alternatives to test: a browser-automation MCP server available to <code dir="ltr">codex exec</code>, or another documented way to reach the active Codex task. If neither works, report the boundary as unresolved.</td></tr><tr><td>Packet parts truncated or reordered in the Claude app</td><td>R4</td><td>Synthesis from partial record</td><td>Per-part digests, end marker, <code dir="ltr">receipt_incomplete</code>, re-fetch. Stage 0(c).</td></tr><tr><td>Prompt injection from packet text into King or Normal tool calls</td><td>R5, R8</td><td>Forged decree or request</td><td>Scope separation, receipt-bound decree, human-tap sovereign actions, decree text shown in status before release.</td></tr><tr><td>Normal’s intake conversation and ChatGPT history shape its later proposals</td><td>R7</td><td>Exposure mislabelled as independence</td><td>Manifest declares the intake conversation; status carries no contribution bodies; proposals stay in fresh conversations driven by the Right Hand.</td></tr><tr><td>Courier crash during execution</td><td>R6</td><td>Double or lost execution</td><td>Lease, journal, reconcile before re-run.</td></tr><tr><td>Relay unreachable or ledger and remote disagree</td><td>R3</td><td>False “all good” status</td><td>The relay returns an error and Normal reports status unavailable; status shows when the relay last verified the remote and fails closed on mismatch.</td></tr><tr><td>Relay compromise</td><td>R5</td><td>Forged records</td><td>OAuth with separate clients and scopes, read-only GitHub token, and the courier accepting only decrees whose ledger record chain validates. A compromised relay is an unaddressed residual risk.</td></tr><tr><td>PC off</td><td>R1, R3</td><td>No execution</td><td>Requests stay <code dir="ltr">submitted</code>; status says “accepted by relay, not claimed, PC current state unconfirmed”. No wake-up is added, per U2.</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<p dir="ltr" data-cds-heading=""><strong>Refutation tests</strong></p>
<ol dir="ltr">
<li><strong>Write probe.</strong> If a write tool call from the ChatGPT phone app is refused or not offered on Martim’s account, I abandon direct intake in favour of the link-tap fallback.</li>
<li><strong>Headless browser probe.</strong> If a <code dir="ltr">codex exec</code> session started by the courier cannot perform a browser action in a fresh page, the PC trigger as designed is not established, and I withdraw the recommendation until another start mechanism is shown.</li>
<li><strong>Packet ingestion probe.</strong> If the Claude phone app does not return all parts with matching digests, I change to manual attachment for the King handoff.</li>
<li><strong>Duplication probe.</strong> Submit the same request twice and the same decree twice. Anything other than one debate and one execution refutes the idempotency design.</li>
<li><strong>Authority probe.</strong> Ask Opus, in the Claude app, to create a veto record. If the relay accepts it, the scope separation fails and the design is wrong.</li>
</ol>

## capturas/sonnet-review-rendered.html

<div data-perf-reply-text="" class="_blocks_4za3l_47 standard-markdown grid-cols-1 grid [&amp;_&gt;_*]:min-w-0 whitespace-normal break-words print:block"><p dir="ltr">END-OF-PACKET-003-REVIEW-v1 | Missing sections: none</p>
<h2 dir="ltr">Review — sonnet</h2>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li><strong>Participant:</strong> sonnet.</li>
<li><strong>Visible model:</strong> Sonnet 5.5 per the session configuration. The interface label is not visible to me and is not independently attested.</li>
<li><strong>Date:</strong> 2026-10-17.</li>
<li><strong>Phase and round:</strong> Cross review / round 02.</li>
<li><strong>Context version:</strong> v1 (debate 003-mobile-bridge).</li>
<li><strong>Reference commit:</strong> source baseline <code dir="ltr">95d853ba7480260d5a9c4b8541b4b1b32a6d90f3</code>; governance <code dir="ltr">389a4367de088361adcaeec271fb438c6fb0b492</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Files received and read:</strong> all sixteen listed sections, in the stated order and in full: LEIS, REGRAS, CONTEXTO, OPERATING-MODEL, MANIFESTO, CONTRIBUICAO template, the five proposals, sonnet.incomplete.md, the three link captures, FIXED-PHASE-PROMPT. None partial.</li>
<li><strong>Tools used:</strong> none. I retrieved no documentation in this phase, so no external capability claim below was independently verified. Each is carried as <code dir="ltr">attributed</code>, <code dir="ltr">contested</code> or <code dir="ltr">unknown</code>.</li>
<li><strong>Cross-conversation memory:</strong> an account-level memory snapshot exists in this deployment. Nothing in it concerns this debate and I did not use it.</li>
<li><strong>Prior exposure:</strong> this packet only. The packet contains <code dir="ltr">propostas/sonnet.md</code> and <code dir="ltr">sonnet.incomplete.md</code>, labelled as sonnet’s. I do not recognize them from this conversation, since it is new, so I cannot confirm authorship. Their content is consistent with the participant ID, and I review them by the same standard as the others.</li>
<li><strong>New conversation:</strong> yes, as far as I can observe. The packet and routing line were the first content.</li>
<li><strong>Access limits:</strong>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li>No phone, account or PC inspection.</li>
<li>Rendered captures carry interface artifacts: argon’s “MD” and “+ 1” labels, argon table cells cut mid-text, and a stray citation fragment inside sonnet.incomplete.md.</li>
<li>Normal’s capture has no link list, so its external sources cannot be traced to URLs.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 dir="ltr">Brief</h3>
<p dir="ltr"><strong>Position, not a plan.</strong> Keep what the proposals share:</p>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li>an outbound-only PC worker;</li>
<li>an append-only operational ledger bound to debate and revision;</li>
<li>Git as the artifact record;</li>
<li>a plan-commit-then-decree handshake;</li>
<li>Martim-authenticated origin attestation before any decree executes.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="ltr">Treat every phone-side adapter as a candidate that must pass a probe in the exact intended conversation before it is chosen. The candidates are a native tool in the GPT-6 Normal conversation, a Claude remote connector, Drive/Gmail, and an explicit relay page.</p>
<p dir="ltr" data-cds-heading=""><strong>Decisive reasons:</strong></p>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li>No proposal establishes a phone-side read or write path in the intended conversations.</li>
<li>The ChatGPT-side evidence conflicts: sol, normal and astra cite a help page saying custom MCP is web-only, while sonnet cites an SDK page saying connectors reach mobile once linked on web.</li>
<li>The choice is therefore decided by authority and recovery, where sol, normal and astra are strongest, and by surface fidelity, where astra and sonnet are strongest.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="ltr" data-cds-heading=""><strong>Blocking defects:</strong></p>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li>sonnet and argon both produce decrees that cannot cite the plan’s commit, contrary to REGRAS “Decision”.</li>
<li>argon’s transport depends on UI polling, its fallback replaces the specified entry surface, and its status path has no fallback.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="ltr"><strong>Main alternative:</strong> argon’s browser-sync design, the only one needing no new connector. It fails if conversation sync or unattended browser control is unreliable. MANIFESTO records a Work setting that disabled the browser tool, and a clipboard that returned empty then stale content.</p>
<p dir="ltr"><strong>Decisive check:</strong> probe in the exact Normal and Opus phone conversations, and run an unattended Right Hand start that reaches a web participant.</p>
<h3 dir="ltr">Analysis</h3>
<h4 dir="ltr">1. Per-proposal review</h4>
<h5 dir="ltr">sol (<code dir="ltr">propostas/sol.md</code>)</h5>
<p dir="ltr" data-cds-heading=""><strong>Strengths to keep</strong></p>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li>It separates the manual baseline from the native-tool alternative and refuses to claim an unverified Normal path.</li>
<li>Authority and revisions are carried in server-set fields. A payload saying <code dir="ltr">actor: King</code> grants nothing.</li>
<li>The two-step plan-commit-then-decree sequence satisfies REGRAS.</li>
<li>Martim’s origin attestation is bound to exact bytes.</li>
<li>A veto or amendment supersedes pending execution, with <code dir="ltr">outcome_unknown</code> reconciliation for in-flight effects.</li>
<li>The state list separates <code dir="ltr">current_unavailable</code> from last-known state.</li>
<li>The refutation tests are concrete, including a forged King document and a repeated decree.</li>
</ul>

<h5 dir="ltr">normal (<code dir="ltr">propostas/normal.md</code>)</h5>
<p dir="ltr" data-cds-heading=""><strong>Strengths to keep</strong></p>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li>It names a documented receiving primitive, the Drive change feed, so the PC needs no inbound listener. Detection of changes is by polling with page tokens.</li>
<li>It reads the published packet back and compares it with frozen originals, which guards against Google Docs conversion altering text.</li>
<li>Folder-level permissions separate the request inbox from read-only status and synthesis.</li>
<li>The envelope and message-type table is clear, the journal is local and transactional, and the plan/decree sequence is correct.</li>
<li>The attestation endpoint uses a one-use challenge bound to the decree digest.</li>
<li>It explicitly refuses to treat provider identity as authorship.</li>
</ul>

<li>A courier lease plus a local journal.</li>
<li>The analysis of why <code dir="ltr">@codex</code> cloud tasks break R2.</li>
<li>Contested and unknown claims labelled as such.</li>
</ul>

<h5 dir="ltr">astra (<code dir="ltr">propostas/astra.md</code>)</h5>
<p dir="ltr" data-cds-heading=""><strong>Strengths to keep</strong></p>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li>It separates authentication from authorship attestation and binds the attestation to digest, handoff and conversation reference.</li>
<li>It keeps four state dimensions (Council phase, delivery, operation, connectivity), so a disconnected worker does not erase the recorded phase.</li>
<li>A completed Codex turn is not treated as Council completion.</li>
<li>It adds an execution-to-King-review contract.</li>
<li>It has a <code dir="ltr">reconciliation_required</code> state.</li>
<li>It insists that the exact phone conversation and model pass the test, with no renaming of another surface as “Normal”.</li>
<li>Its honest manual-relay alternative stays within the specified surfaces.</li>
</ul>

<h4 dir="ltr">2. Comparison against requirements and criteria</h4>
<p dir="ltr" data-cds-heading=""><strong>Design discriminators</strong></p>
<div dir="ltr" class="md-table-scroll prose-scroll print:overflow-x-visible"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col" style="">Dimension</th><th scope="col" style="">sol</th><th scope="col" style="">normal</th><th scope="col" style="">argon</th><th scope="col" style="">sonnet</th><th scope="col" style="">astra</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Phone → PC</td><td>Paste into an authenticated relay form</td><td>ChatGPT writes a Drive document</td><td>PC polls the intake conversation</td><td>MCP tool in ChatGPT</td><td>GPT Action</td></tr><tr><td>State → phone</td><td>Martim pastes a snapshot</td><td>Drive read</td><td>Snapshots posted into the thread</td><td><code dir="ltr">get_status</code> tool</td><td>Action status call</td></tr><tr><td>Synthesis → Claude</td><td>Remote connector, attachment fallback</td><td>Drive document, manual open</td><td>PC drives the Claude web thread</td><td>MCP parts</td><td>Remote connector</td></tr><tr><td>Decree → PC</td><td>Connector or upload, attested</td><td>Gmail, attested</td><td>Scraped from Claude web</td><td>MCP submit, release gate</td><td>Connector, attested</td></tr><tr><td>PC trigger</td><td>Windows worker plus app server</td><td>Drive change feed plus worker</td><td>Daemon</td><td>Courier plus <code dir="ltr">codex exec</code></td><td>Supervisor plus app server</td></tr><tr><td>Authority root</td><td>Martim attestation</td><td>Martim attestation</td><td>Pinned conversation plus nonce</td><td>Scope plus release tap</td><td>Martim attestation</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<p dir="ltr" data-cds-heading=""><strong>R#, by design</strong></p>
<div dir="ltr" class="md-table-scroll prose-scroll print:overflow-x-visible"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col" style="">R#</th><th scope="col" style="">sol</th><th scope="col" style="">normal</th><th scope="col" style="">argon</th><th scope="col" style="">sonnet</th><th scope="col" style="">astra</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>R1</td><td>met</td><td>met</td><td>unverified</td><td>met</td><td>met</td></tr><tr><td>R2</td><td>met</td><td>met</td><td>met</td><td>met</td><td>met</td></tr><tr><td>R3</td><td>unverified</td><td>unverified</td><td>unverified</td><td>met</td><td>met</td></tr><tr><td>R4</td><td>met</td><td>met</td><td>met</td><td>met</td><td>met</td></tr><tr><td>R5</td><td>met</td><td>met</td><td>broken</td><td>broken</td><td>met</td></tr><tr><td>R6</td><td>met</td><td>met</td><td>met</td><td>met</td><td>met</td></tr><tr><td>R7</td><td>met</td><td>met</td><td>met</td><td>met</td><td>met</td></tr><tr><td>R8</td><td>met</td><td>unverified</td><td>unverified</td><td>unverified</td><td>met</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
<p dir="ltr">These codes assess the design against the requirement as written. Capability dependencies appear under U1 and R8, and in the Evidence table.</p>
<p dir="ltr" data-cds-heading=""><strong>By priority</strong></p>
<ol dir="ltr">
<li><strong>Authority and complete delivery.</strong>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li>sol, normal and astra are strongest. Each has the plan-commit-then-decree handshake and an attestation bound to the exact digest.</li>
<li>sonnet has the best launch authorization but loses points on ordering and on scope-as-role.</li>
<li>argon is weakest, because it has no attestation and executes on capture.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Demonstrated capability.</strong>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li>argon rests on operations Debate 002 demonstrated, but its sync assumption is unestablished and MANIFESTO records the browser tool failing.</li>
<li>The others rest on documented but unverified connectors.</li>
<li>sol, astra and sonnet each name the unverified Codex tool-parity dependency. argon, which keeps browser control on the PC, does not.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>State and recovery.</strong>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li>astra’s four dimensions and sonnet’s server-side <code dir="ltr">pc_current</code> are the clearest.</li>
<li>Every proposal except argon has a reconciliation state for uncertain effects.</li>
<li>argon’s write-ahead log addresses the same problem differently.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Fit to surfaces.</strong>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li>sonnet, astra and argon answer status directly in Normal.</li>
<li>sol keeps Normal but needs manual transfers.</li>
<li>normal keeps Normal but adds Drive and Gmail.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ol>
<p dir="ltr">No proposal estimates cost, effort or resources, apart from the minor phrase in sonnet-R02-10.</p>
<h4 dir="ltr">3. Current recommendation</h4>
<p dir="ltr" data-cds-heading=""><strong>What I would carry forward</strong></p>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li><strong>A transport-independent contract layer.</strong> This means:
<ul dir="ltr">
<li>an envelope with debate, revision, idempotency key and payload digest;</li>
<li>authenticated principal supplied by the server, never by payload text;</li>
<li>append-only records, and separate state dimensions;</li>
<li>freshness computed at read time;</li>
<li>a <code dir="ltr">reconciliation_required</code> or <code dir="ltr">outcome_unknown</code> state for interrupted effects.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Authority.</strong> Authentication is not authorship. Before any decree executes, Martim authenticates an attestation bound to the exact digest and conversation reference. His veto and amendment are separate records created only through his authenticated action.</li>
<li><strong>Sequence.</strong> The sequence runs plan, commit, return the commit reference to the King, decree citing it, then execution and King review.</li>
<li><strong>Context.</strong> A launch authorization bound to a context commit is carried forward, unless Martim states otherwise (sonnet-R02-19).</li>
<li><strong>Phone-edge adapters.</strong> Each is a candidate that must pass a probe in the exact conversation:
<ul dir="ltr">
<li>a native read/write tool in GPT-6 Normal;</li>
<li>a Claude remote connector;</li>
<li>Drive/Gmail;</li>
<li>the sol relay-page baseline, kept as a labelled fallback.<br>
No adapter replaces a specified surface without Martim’s instruction.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>PC trigger.</strong> An outbound-only worker, with “required tools and settings present” as a checked precondition and a visible blocked state (sonnet-R02-17).</li>
<li><strong>From argon.</strong> Keep the Stage 0 report, the lease idea (computed at read time), the canary exposure test and the parser separation. Keep browser-sync as a probe candidate, not as the primary trigger.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="ltr" data-cds-heading=""><strong>Decisive gaps raised by one proposal</strong></p>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li><strong>astra (surface fidelity).</strong> The ChatGPT adapter must run in the GPT-6 Normal conversation, and a custom GPT or another model must not be renamed “Normal”. This holds. It also applies to every ChatGPT-side adapter in the other proposals, including mine.</li>
<li><strong>argon (liveness lease).</strong> Valid, but it needs a clock the model may not have (sonnet-R02-18).</li>
<li><strong>normal (Drive change feed plus readback).</strong> A documented receiving primitive, usable if Normal’s Drive write and Claude’s return path are verified. Their state is unknown.</li>
<li><strong>This review (sonnet-R02-17).</strong> The only evidence the packet holds about unattended browser availability is the MANIFESTO episode. No proposal addresses it.</li>
</ul>
<h4 dir="ltr">4. What I would keep or change in my own proposal</h4>
<p dir="ltr" data-cds-heading=""><strong>Keep</strong></p>
<ul dir="ltr">
<li>The relay-plus-courier shape.</li>
<li>Separate OAuth clients and scopes.</li>
<li>The Stage 0 probes.</li>
<li>The launch confirmation bound to a commit.</li>
<li>Receipt matching.</li>
<li>Server-side <code dir="ltr">pc_current</code>.</li>
<li>The journal and reconcile-before-rerun rule.</li>
<li>The <code dir="ltr">@codex</code> analysis.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="ltr" data-cds-heading=""><strong>Change</strong></p>
<ol dir="ltr">
<li>Add the plan-commit-then-decree two-step (sonnet-R02-13).</li>
<li>Add Martim’s origin attestation and stop treating scope as role (sonnet-R02-14).</li>
<li>Downgrade the mobile-connector row to <code dir="ltr">contested</code>. Add the exact-conversation probe, including the model label, and sol’s relay-page baseline as a named fallback (sonnet-R02-15).</li>
<li>Add a Stage 0 check of the browser setting and an explicit blocked state (sonnet-R02-17).</li>
<li>State the release-gate rule as a premise for Martim, with both modes supported (sonnet-R02-16).</li>
<li>Replace mirror-sourced claims with primary pages, or leave them <code dir="ltr">attributed</code>.</li>
</ol>

You are the King (Opus) of the Council. Follow LEIS.md first, then REGRAS.md. Martim alone makes the Laws and may overrule your decree. Participants advise; you decide. The Right Hand operates and implements; you review its work.

On the first line, repeat the packet's end marker and list any missing sections, or write «Missing sections: none». Confirm the marker and every listed section. If anything is missing, ask for the complete packet before issuing a decree. Identify the closed sets and the context version you read.

Declare the visible model (or «not visible»), tools actually used, cross-conversation memory, prior exposure to this debate and whether this is a fresh conversation. Declare your own origin and role conflicts, including any contribution or material you authored.

Apply Law No. 1. Set aside any passage that breaks a Law. List its source, passage and breach in the plan, and reason as if it did not exist. Never recommend changing a Law. If a Law blocks a requirement, say so in one sentence and leave that question to Martim.

Follow every point of REGRAS.md, «Synthesis»:

1. Compare the options against the context's requirements and criteria. Never decide by vote, support count or model reputation. Examine a decisive gap even when only one participant raises it.
2. Write the decision table: D#, decision, related R#, alternatives rejected and reasons, supporting IDs and reversal condition.
3. Write the evidence table. A claim can support a D# only if it appears there with its state, provenance and passage, phase and scope. Use supported, attributed, assumption, contested or unknown. Repetition does not change a state.
4. Carry every blocking and material review ID into the objection ledger. Keep the target, faithful summary and original severity. Assign RESOLVED, CONDITIONAL, OPEN, REFUTED or NOT MATERIAL, with a reason and a place in the plan. A refutation must answer the actual failure condition.
5. Preserve material dissent and explain decisions against prevailing positions.
6. Mark every new premise introduced by the synthesis as pending. State which decision depends on it and how to answer it.
7. State your own origin and role conflicts.
8. Give stages with deliverables, dependencies and observable acceptance checks. Explain how combined components fit together.
9. Set the plan's status to Decreed or Undecided. If the basis is insufficient, state exactly what is missing, how to obtain it and which decision depends on it.
